class.name: NetwMultiplayerCore
class.brief_description: The session, and the owner of one core per plane for the session's whole life.
class.description: A plane's interface reads its core from here rather than constructing one, so an interface and the session it belongs to cannot come to disagree about which records are live. [member channel_book], [member clock_handle], [member scene_core], [member interest_engine], [member liveness_core] and [member lagcomp_core] are all held for that reason: every one of them outlives the interface that writes to it. It is a multiplayer API so that it can eventually be installed as one. The bands that reach a node, a script or the wire are not here yet, and the verbs carrying them refuse rather than answer, because an API that silently accepted an rpc or a configuration would drop it, and a dropped registration reads exactly like one that was never made.

method.name: advance_frame
method.description: Advances the frame a received payload is stamped with while no clock is configured. It advances AFTER intake, so a payload read during a poll carries the frame it arrived in rather than the one after it.

method.name: authored_desired_role
method.description: The role the embedding currently AUTHORS as its intent, read live through the [Callable] installed by [method set_desired_role_reader]. This is not the session machine's own desired role, set through [method session_set_desired_role], and the two are deliberately separate facts. That one is a SNAPSHOT, pushed at the edges that resolve a role so the machine can split a server peer without holding a configuration. This is the authored value as it stands right now, which a caller outside those edges needs when the configuration may have been re-authored since the last one. They agree wherever an edge has just run, and a caller that wants the live fact must ask here, because agreeing today is not the same as being one fact. With no reader installed, or a reader that answers something other than a [enum Role], this answers [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER], which is the role an unconfigured session already intends.

method.name: carrier_append
method.description: Adds one frame to [param peer]'s run, sending whatever run it displaces. Answers the sequence that displaced datagram went out under, and [code]-1[/code] when nothing was displaced, when what went out was reliable, and when the send was refused. None of the three has a sequence to stage against.

method.name: carrier_clear
method.description: Drops every run still held without sending any of it.

method.name: carrier_flush
method.description: Sends every run still held, unreliable lane first. Answers the peer and the sequence of each unreliable datagram that went out, flat and in pairs, which is what a pass staged this tick has to be told before an acknowledgement for that sequence can promote anything.

method.name: carrier_pending
method.description: How many bytes of frames [param peer]'s run on the named lane is holding.

method.name: channel_aggregates
method.description: Whether a frame on [param channel] waits for a flush instead of leaving now. The channel declaration answers it, so the policy is one table rather than a list a sender and a declaration can come to disagree about. [param requested] is the sender's own ask, which the declaration may refuse.

method.name: claim_verdict_warning
method.description: Whether this is the first warning for [param verdict] on [param route] together. Asking claims it, so every later occurrence of the same pair is suppressed and one peer retrying cannot flood a log however often it does.

method.name: clear_seq_books
method.description: Drops every peer's send, inbound, ack and echo sequences.

method.name: clear_verdicts
method.description: Drops every counted total and every claimed warning.

method.name: connect_once
method.description: Wires [param callback] to [param signal] unless that exact pair is already wired, and answers whether the edge is connected once this returns. Arming an edge is therefore idempotent, so a caller re-entering its own setup neither asks first nor doubles the callback. Two [Callable]s that name the same method but carry different bound arguments are different pairs and each connects on its own. A connection the engine refuses counts [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] against the gate partition and answers [code]false[/code], because an edge that silently fails to wire reads exactly like one that never fires.

method.name: count_received
method.description: Counts one inbound datagram of [param bytes] body bytes into [member received_packets] and [member received_bytes].

method.name: count_sent
method.description: Counts one outbound packet and its [param bytes] together. A packet always carries its own byte count, so the pair advances in one verb. Two counters raised at four separate call sites drift the moment one of them forgets its second line.

method.name: count_standalone_ack_out
method.description: Counts one acknowledgement that had no datagram of its own to ride. It raises the outbound state-acknowledgement counter too, so the standalone count can never exceed it.

method.name: count_state_ack_in
method.description: Counts one inbound state ack into [member state_acks_in].

method.name: count_state_ack_out
method.description: Counts one outbound state ack into [member state_acks_out].

method.name: count_verdict
method.description: Counts one [param verdict] on [param route] against the gate partition and answers whether it landed in the partition at all. [constant @GlobalScope.OK] and every value outside the partition count as nothing and answer [code]false[/code]. A route a watcher wants also emits the row as an event.

method.name: datagram_budget
method.description: How many bytes of frames one unreliable datagram may carry. The transport's own ceiling less the headroom the carrier header and the transport's command bytes take, floored so a pathologically small setting still admits one frame rather than refusing every send.

method.name: display_absorb_recovery
method.description: Absorbs one reconciliation into a chasing display: each channel named by [param deltas] seeds its offset with the negated pose change, so the visual stays where it was and glides onto the corrected body. A recovery RESETS its channel's offset rather than accumulating into it, so a correction train cannot wind the visual up. A [param teleported] recovery clears every offset instead, because a genuine desync should be seen to snap. Clamped by the entity's own teleport tier, read through the [Callable] installed by [method set_display_chase_clamp]. A runtime that is no longer chasing drops the recovery, so a signal that arrives after a role change cannot seed an offset nothing will decay.

method.name: display_authors_streams
method.description: Whether every sync channel feeding this entity's tracked values is authored by THIS peer, so no receive stream exists to play back and the display must sample the local simulation instead. Answered by the session's installed authorship reader, because deciding it needs the property sets and the synchronizer visibility rules. With none installed the answer is [code]false[/code], which is the safe reading: an entity with no known authorship plays back rather than samples.

method.name: display_chase_smooth_time
method.description: The exponential time a chasing display eases toward the live body over, in seconds. The runtime's own [constant NetwDisplayDecl.PARAM_PREDICTED_SMOOTH_TIME] when it is set, and otherwise most of one tick derived from [member NetwDisplayTiming.ticktime], so an entity that declares nothing still eases at a rate its tickrate justifies.

method.name: display_ensure_state
method.description: The one constructor for every channel shape, and the only place a channel's port, lane and history are wired. A channel whose [param source_prop] is empty is an event-argument channel: it has no source and writes [param target_prop] where it stands. One with a source samples it, and aims at the runtime's visual root when the entity declares one. Declaring a channel whose key already exists updates the standing channel's shape and answers it, so re-declaring an entity never doubles its channels or drops the history it has already collected.

method.name: display_pump_entity
method.description: Advances one entity's display by one frame, selected by its flat handle rather than by its runtime. Refuses with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when no runtime answers for [param entity], and with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when [param timing] is null, which is what a pump that ran before any clock configurator registered looks like.

method.name: display_pump_runtime
method.description: Advances one display runtime by one frame and counts it into [param stats], defaulting to the book's own record. Dispatches on [member NetwDisplayRuntime.pump_mode]: [constant NetwDisplayDecl.PUMP_CHASE] eases the visual toward the live body, [constant NetwDisplayDecl.PUMP_DISABLED] declines without counting, and everything else samples the recorded history under the playhead. A runtime still reading [constant NetwDisplayDecl.PUMP_UNRESOLVED] is resolved first, through the [Callable] installed by [method set_display_role_resolver]. Resolution is the only step that needs a body, so a runtime whose owner is gone declines to resolve rather than following a freed pointer, while a runtime that already knows its mode pumps without one. That is what lets a rig drive the real kernels with no scene tree at all.

method.name: display_rebuild_runtime
method.description: Rebuilds one entity's channel table from what its authoring registry declares, then leaves the runtime unresolved so the next pass decides its role afresh. REPLACES the table rather than adding to it, because a rebuild answers "what does this entity display now" and an entity that has been re-declared must not accumulate the channels it used to have. A runtime with no entity or no live owner is left alone: there is nothing to read a declaration from.

method.name: display_wants_runtime
method.description: Whether [param owner] declares anything worth displaying: any interpolated property, RPC or signal argument in its subtree, or a physics body that a remote display has to freeze. An entity that declares none never builds a runtime at all, which is what keeps the pump proportional to what is actually smoothed rather than to how many entities exist.

method.name: effect_adopt
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwEffectLedger.adopt] on [method get_effect_ledger].

method.name: effect_arm
method.description: Arms the optimistic act [param key], parking [param revert] against a deadline. The deadline is the session's own tick plus [param timeout_ticks], so an act armed during a pump expires a whole wait later rather than at whatever tick a caller happened to read first. Zero takes the session default.

method.name: effect_count
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwEffectLedger.count] on [method get_effect_ledger].

method.name: effect_discard
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwEffectLedger.discard] on [method get_effect_ledger].

method.name: effect_pending
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwEffectLedger.pending] on [method get_effect_ledger].

method.name: effect_sweep
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwEffectLedger.sweep] on [method get_effect_ledger].

method.name: effect_watch
method.description: Watches the armed act [param key], answering [code]false[/code] when it is not armed. A watcher can therefore never outlive the act it observes.

method.name: entity_announce_reparented
method.description: The settled half of [method entity_settle_reparented], announcing [code]reparented[/code] on [param wrapper]. An owner that is gone or no longer in the tree is not reported at all, because the settle runs after the propagation and a report naming a node the listener cannot read is worse than none.

method.name: entity_at_or_above
method.description: The nearest handle at or above [param node], or an invalid [RID] when the walk finds none. The walk is over nodes because that is where the answer lives: an entity marks its root with [code]netw_entity[/code] metadata, so the nearest marked ancestor is the nearest entity.

method.name: entity_broadcast_control
method.description: Fans a settled controller to the peers that can see the entity. Off-session there is no plane to fan through, and that is the ordinary case rather than an error: every offline rig takes it on every transfer.

method.name: entity_control_request
method.description: Asks the server to hand this peer control of [param entity]. The ask carries no payload, because the route names the subject and the transport names the asker. The server decides, and a peer that gets control learns it from the answer rather than from having asked.

method.name: entity_derived_binding
method.description: The derived set binding of [param record] kind on [param owner], or [code]null[/code]. The owner's own marks win, then [param route]'s derived group answers a set a child node declares, such as an input mark living on a component under the root. Resolved per call, so a reparent is followed for free, matching how the retained lane and the pump re-resolve route per pass. A session told of no replication plane resolves nothing.

method.name: entity_derived_group
method.description: Every derived set binding declared on [param route], on any of its nodes.

method.name: entity_describe
method.description: What this session holds about [param route], as one read a watcher can put beside an event record. [codeblock] { ┠╴route int the route asked about ┠╴entity_id StringName the durable label ┠╴peer_id int the peer this entity represents, 0 for a server-owned one ┠╴stage int a [enum NetwEntity.Stage] value ┠╴controller int the peer that steers it, 0 for the server ┠╴liveness int a [enum NetwLivenessCore.State] value ┖╴layers Array the interest layers it belongs to, in join order } [/codeblock] Empty for a route this session holds no record for. A lifecycle event names its subject and not its state, because attaching a projection to every event costs every session that emits one. This is the read that answers the state, and [constant DESPAWNED] carries the last one instead, since a route outlives its entity by exactly one event.

method.name: entity_enter_tree
method.description: What a tree entry does to an entity: hydrate the identity, classify it, arm it, take a route, announce it, wire the node's own signals, and go live. A first entry classifies the record and goes live. A reparent re-entry keeps its live stage and only reapplies authority and scene registration for the new parent, so it is not a second birth. An entry the record classifies as inert, a template or a bare programmatic node, stops there. The order matters and is the whole reason this is one verb: identity, then control authority, then scene registration.

method.name: entity_free_owner
method.description: Frees [param owner]. The act a linger schedules, bound to the session rather than free-standing because a callable with no object reads as invalid and the settle queue skips those.

method.name: entity_governs_property
method.description: Whether a stream other than [param exclude] already drives the live target [param path] names under [param owner]. A persisted client-owned field that another stream drives is a double-authority mistake, and this is what flags it. [param exclude] exists because a stream is not competition with itself. Both halves are checked: every other [MultiplayerSynchronizer] on the owner, and every field a derived binding on [param route] declares.

method.name: entity_instantiate_copy
method.description: An unparented copy of [param template_node]'s scene, carrying NO marked spawn state, because the marks are resolved through a session or not at all. [param configure] runs on the copy's wrapper before the copy enters any tree.

method.name: entity_instantiate_from
method.description: An unparented copy of [param template_node]'s scene, carrying every marked value [method set_spawn_state_gather] names, resolved onto the copy's counterpart of each source node. A source the copy has no counterpart for is skipped rather than written onto the root. [param configure] runs on the copy's wrapper, which exists by then, because a caller configures the entity rather than the node.

method.name: entity_instantiate_player
method.description: An unparented copy of [param owner]'s scene bound to [param participant]'s identity. A participant that names no join has not been accepted, so it names no player to build one for and this answers [code]null[/code].

method.name: entity_linger
method.description: Deactivates [param owner] at once and frees it [param pumps] pumps later, which is what keeps a despawned target rewindable for a window a record plane with no tree counts as well as a rendered one does. The record and its owner are named by the caller rather than resolved from the session's index, because an entity is stamped with the session it belongs to before that session has adopted it.

method.name: entity_move
method.description: The node half of a reparent, which is all a record no session holds can have: the destination pose, the ready reset, and the move itself. [param record] carries the move as [member NetwEntityRecord.reparenting] for the duration, so an [code]_exit_tree[/code] consumer can tell a reparent from a despawn. An owner that no parent holds is added rather than moved, because [method Node.reparent] needs a parent to move away from.

method.name: entity_of
method.description: The entity handle [param node] stands for, adopting the record on the way. It is an adopt over the record at or above [param node], which is one verb rather than two because every caller wanted both halves, and a caller that took only the first would hold a handle the index does not.

method.name: entity_parent_of
method.description: The nearest ancestor handle of [param entity], or an invalid [RID] at a root. The walk is over nodes because that is where the answer lives: an entity marks its root, so the nearest marked ancestor is the nearest entity. It answers in handles because a caller asked about one.

method.name: entity_reparent
method.description: Moves [param owner] under [param new_parent], carrying its admission edge when [method entity_reparent_crosses] says the move leaves one scene for another. Admission moves BEFORE the reparent, so the destination's row is already flushed when the subtree's spawn packets go out. Membership itself needs no handoff: it is ancestry, and the new parent is the whole of it. A refused move leaves nothing in flight, because a record still holding one would read every later tree exit as a reparent and keep a dead route alive. The record and its owner are named by the caller for the same reason [method entity_linger]'s are.

method.name: entity_reparent_crosses
method.description: Whether moving [param entity] under [param destination] carries a player across a scene boundary, which is the only move that has to carry an admission edge as well as a parent. All three terms are needed: a server-owned entity is admitted nowhere, a destination under no declared scene has no boundary to admit to, and a destination inside the scene the player is already in re-sends an edge it already holds.

method.name: entity_request_control
method.description: Asks [param plane] to carry a control request for [param wrapper]. With no peer connected there is no server to route the ask to, so the request is decided where it was made instead of being dropped.

method.name: entity_scene_facet
method.description: The scene facet [param record]'s entity BELONGS to, which is its nearest declaring ancestor's, or its own when no scene resolves. Self-inclusive, so an entity that declares a scene answers itself. It resolves through [method entity_scene_of] rather than repeating the walk, so a caller asking which scene an entity is in and one asking which handle to announce cannot come to disagree. The record and its wrapper are named by the caller rather than resolved from the index, because an entity is asked which scene it is in before this session has adopted it, and one the index does not hold still belongs to a scene: its own.

method.name: entity_scene_of
method.description: The nearest handle at or above [param entity] whose record declares a scene, or an invalid [RID]. At-or-above, because a scene container is its own scene.

method.name: entity_settle_reparented
method.description: Reports a move at this session's next settle rather than inside the propagation that made it, because the subtree is still rebuilding there and every node is back in the tree by the settle. Unkeyed, because two moves in one cascade are two discontinuities and a consumer resetting its smoothing owes each of them an answer.

method.name: entity_spawn_copy_under
method.description: [method entity_spawn_under]'s seating over a copy carrying no marked spawn state, for a template no session holds.

method.name: entity_spawn_player
method.description: [method entity_instantiate_player]'s copy, handed to [param scene] as one of its players. A participant that builds no player is never seated.

method.name: entity_spawn_under
method.description: A copy of [param owner]'s scene, named after [param id] when one is given, seated under [param parent]. A [param parent] of [code]null[/code] seats the copy beside its template, and a template with neither seats nothing rather than leaking an unparented copy.

method.name: forget_peer_seqs
method.description: Drops [param peer]'s send, inbound, ack and echo sequences, so a peer that has left is forgotten by id rather than by asking a transport that no longer knows it.

method.name: frame_datagram
method.description: The datagram [param payload] rides to [param peer], stamped and booked. One call, because the stamp, the echo it piggybacks, and the record that this peer is no longer owed a standalone acknowledgement are one decision. Split apart, a caller could frame under a sequence it had not asked for yet.

method.name: frame_pack
method.description: One payload wrapped in the frame envelope many frames pack into a datagram by. [codeblock] route varint | comp u8 | channel u8 | len varint | payload [/codeblock] The length prefix is what lets a reader walk a datagram frame by frame, so it counts the payload rather than the frame. [param comp] addresses the target inside the entity: [code]0[/code] is the entity root, [code]1[/code] to [code]254[/code] a row of its component table, and [code]255[/code] means [param path] names an unmapped node. A [code]255[/code] frame carries that path length-prefixed INSIDE the payload, never beside it, because a path written outside the length would read as the next frame.

method.name: get_clock_handle
method.description: The session's clock, minted with the session and running for its whole life. [member NetwMultiplayer.clock] is this object, so a caller holding one never has to re-fetch it after a [MultiplayerClock] registers or leaves.

method.name: get_effect_ledger
method.description: The [NetwEffectLedger] [method effect_arm] and the rest of the [code]effect_*[/code] verbs act on.

method.name: get_inner
method.description: The transport this carrier writes through. A [SceneMultiplayer] rather than the [MultiplayerPeer] under it, because [method SceneMultiplayer.send_bytes] is not a thin wrapper: it prepends the raw command byte the receiving side demuxes on, relays a client-to-client datagram through the server, honours a negative target as broadcast-with-exclusion, and refuses a peer that is not connected.

method.name: get_local_player
method.description: The wrapper this peer is represented by, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: handle_of_wrapper
method.description: The handle [param wrapper] carries, or an invalid [RID] for a wrapper this session never adopted, which is what separates another session's entity from one of ours.

method.name: has_inbound_seq
method.description: Whether this session holds an inbound sequence for [param peer] yet.

method.name: has_wrapper_factory
method.description: Returns whether anything has registered how to build an entity wrapper.

method.name: inbound_seq
method.description: The freshest datagram of [param peer]'s this session holds, undefined when [method has_inbound_seq] answers [code]false[/code].

method.name: interest_awareness_clear
method.description: Drops every queued awareness edge without sending any. This is what a session teardown owes the relay, and what a peer that is not the server does with edges it queued before it learned that.

method.name: interest_awareness_drain
method.description: Takes every queued awareness edge and empties the relay, as one [code][peer_id, wire][/code] row per target peer that has edges waiting. A target whose wire came out empty is left out rather than handed back as an empty row, so a caller may send every row it is given. Draining is unconditional and sending is not: a caller decides per row whether that peer is still reachable, and an edge for a peer it skips is gone rather than requeued. That is the correct trade for awareness, because an edge names a transition that has already happened and a later row supersedes it.

method.name: interest_awareness_forget
method.description: Drops the edges queued for [param peer_id] alone, which is what a disconnect owes: the peer will never read them, and leaving them queued would hand [method interest_awareness_drain] a row no caller can send.

method.name: interest_awareness_queue_layer
method.description: Queues, for [param peer_id], the fact that the entity at [param route] entered or left [param layer_id] from that peer's own point of view. [param kind] is [code]1[/code] for an enter and [code]0[/code] for a leave. The edge is addressed by ROUTE rather than by node path, because the receiving peer may not have spawned the entity yet and a route is the one name that resolves either way. A [param route] of [code]0[/code] is refused, since no receiver could resolve it, and so is a [param peer_id] of [code]0[/code], which names no peer and would leave the edge queued for a drain to hand nobody.

method.name: interest_awareness_queue_observer
method.description: Queues, for [param peer_id], the fact that [param observer_peer] began or stopped seeing the entity at [param route] through [param layer_id]. Where [method interest_awareness_queue_layer] tells a peer about its own sight, this tells an entity's owner about somebody else's. A [param route] of [code]0[/code] and a [param peer_id] of [code]0[/code] are refused for the same reasons.

method.name: interest_bit_admits
method.description: Whether [param entity]'s committed row admits [param peer_bit], the dense bit index a peer id was assigned by [method interest_peer_bit], not the peer id itself. Passing a raw peer id here reads whatever bit happens to share that number rather than that peer's verdict.

method.name: interest_commit
method.description: Publishes the delta staged by [method interest_recompute]: every committed transition is announced to its layer and queued for the peers that need to hear it, the matrix those reads answer from is swapped in, entities that retired during the fold are swept, and local perception is reconciled against the new rows. A call with nothing staged, which is always true on a client, is a no-op.

method.name: interest_committed_row
method.description: The committed admission bitset for [param entity], one bit per known peer at [method interest_peer_bit]'s numbering, packed 63 bits to a word and widened to the same word count as the live-peer row. An entity the matrix never held reads the same all-zero row as one that is held and admits nobody, so a caller that must tell those apart checks [method interest_has_committed_intent] first.

method.name: interest_entity_has_filter
method.description: Whether [param entity] is subject to interest filtering at all, rather than being open to every peer by default. On the server this reads whether [param entity] carries any committed layer membership; off the server it reads whether the local [member NetwEntity.interest] declaration names any label. An entity that answers [code]false[/code] here needs no [method interest_wire_admits] check, because nothing has ever narrowed who receives it.

method.name: interest_explain_bit
method.description: A human-readable reason for [param entity]'s committed verdict at [param peer_bit], the same dense index [method interest_bit_admits] takes. Answers [code]"entity is not registered"[/code] for an entity the matrix never held, which is otherwise indistinguishable from a zero verdict through [method interest_bit_admits] alone.

method.name: interest_flush_key
method.description: The settle key every interest flush request coalesces under, so a cascade of admissions, releases and layer mutations inside one pump settles exactly once and settles after the whole cascade. It is read from here rather than spelled a second time in the interface that schedules under it, because two spellings of one key are two flushes that never coalesce.

method.name: interest_flush_pending
method.description: Whether an interest flush is scheduled and has not run yet. This is what makes a missing flush observable. A stale committed matrix reads as a plausible one, so a caller cannot tell a row that was recomputed from a row that merely happened to be right, and asks whether the flush was REQUESTED instead.

method.name: interest_flush_tail
method.description: Runs the two steps that follow a committed matrix: the awareness batches [method interest_commit] queued are relayed to the peers they address through the [Callable] installed by [method set_interest_awareness_send], and then, while this peer holds a connected multiplayer peer, the [Callable] installed by [method set_interest_visibility_sweep] is asked to reconcile per-peer spawn and despawn against the new admissions. Relaying is a server act and answers nothing without an installed send.

method.name: interest_forget_layer_row
method.description: Erases [param layer_id]'s row from the interest engine: every membership and viewer edge it held, staged for the next [method interest_recompute] to fold into the committed matrix. It leaves the open [NetwInterestLayer] handle for [param layer_id] in place, so a caller that also wants the handle gone still calls [method layer_close].

method.name: interest_has_committed_intent
method.description: Whether [param entity] carries an explicit, committed admission intent rather than the default of admitting every known peer. [method interest_committed_row] cannot distinguish an entity that was never registered from one that is registered but currently admits nobody, since both read as an all-zero row: this is the check that tells them apart.

method.name: interest_has_filter
method.description: Whether [param entity] is subject to a visibility filter at all, which is what lets a send skip the per-peer verdict for an entity nothing narrows. On server authority the answer is the committed row, so an entity no layer names is unfiltered however it was declared. Off the server the committed row is empty until the server admits the entity, so the answer is the entity's own declared labels, read from the interest facet's declaration.

method.name: interest_has_layer
method.description: Whether the interest engine itself has a row for [param layer_id], independent of whether this session still holds an open [NetwInterestLayer] handle for it. [method interest_layer_named] and this method can disagree: [method interest_forget_layer_row] clears the engine's row without closing the handle, and a handle opened through [method interest_layer] declares the row without being asked here first.

method.name: interest_known_peers
method.description: Every peer id the interest matrix has assigned a bit to, in no particular order. This is the peer set [method interest_committed_row] is sized against, not the currently connected peer set.

method.name: interest_layer
method.description: Returns the [NetwInterestLayer] addressed by [param name], opening it in the session's interest engine on first use. A second call with the same [param name] returns a handle to the same layer, so declaring a layer twice never splits its membership.

method.name: interest_layer_named
method.description: Returns the [NetwInterestLayer] already open under [param name], or a null reference if nothing has opened it yet. Unlike [method interest_layer] this never creates one, so it is the read a caller reaches for when opening a layer as a side effect would be wrong.

method.name: interest_layers
method.description: Returns every [NetwInterestLayer] this session currently holds open, in no particular order. A layer [method interest_forget_layer_row] has cleared from the interest engine still appears here until [method layer_close] releases its handle.

method.name: interest_leave_commit
method.description: Acknowledges the layer exits [method interest_leave_resolve] read for [param entity] and [param peer_id], then applies [param decision]: a despawn, or [param forced], drops the retained copy outright; otherwise the copy is retained and every CUSTOM action in [param decision] is called with [param peer_id] and its layer id. [param forced] is for a peer the session is dropping outright, where the custom actions never run.

method.name: interest_leave_finish_sweep
method.description: Drops every leave attribution the spawn pipeline recorded but never carried through [method interest_leave_resolve] and [method interest_leave_commit] in the pass now ending, so an exit no plan consumed cannot leak into the next sweep.

method.name: interest_leave_resolve
method.description: Computes the wire verdict for [param entity] leaving [param peer_id]'s admitted set, without committing anything. For every layer the last interest flush recorded as no longer admitting the pair, the leave policy comes from [param entity]'s own declaration first and the layer's [member NetwInterestLayer.default_leave_policy] second: a DESPAWN on any layer wins outright, and every CUSTOM layer contributes its callback and layer id. With no such layer, the verdict is despawn unless the pair is already retained from an earlier resolve. Returns: [codeblock] { ┠╴ despawn: bool # true means send a despawn frame ┖╴ custom: Array # [callback, layer_id] pairs to run on commit } [/codeblock] The spawn pipeline calls this while planning a peer's row, and the returned [Dictionary] is only real once [method interest_leave_commit] is given the decision that was acted on.

method.name: interest_membership_ids
interest_monitor_snapshot
method.description: Aggregate occupancy and churn counters for the whole interest plane. [codeblock] { ┠╴ layers: int # declared layer count ┠╴ entities_filtered: int # entities carrying membership ┠╴ visible_edges: int # admitted (entity, peer) pairs ┠╴ dirty_entities: int # entities awaiting the next flush ┠╴ relay_backlog: int # pending liveness relay work ┠╴ transitions_total: int # summed enter plus exit since startup ┖╴ vanished_dirty_skips: int # dirty entities skipped because they left first } [/codeblock] [code]transitions_total[/code] and [code]vanished_dirty_skips[/code] are cumulative, so a monitor reads them as a delta over an interval to surface churn.

method.name: interest_participant_sees
method.description: Whether [param peer_id] can see [param entity] as an ordinary participant, holding a listen-server host to the same rule as any client. On the server this reads [param peer_id]'s committed bit off [method interest_committed_row]; off the server it can only answer for the local peer, from the projection of its own [member NetwEntity.interest] declaration. Gameplay that asks "can this participant see that entity" calls here; a send gate that must never blind the server to its own entities calls [method interest_wire_admits] instead.

method.name: interest_peer_bit
method.description: The dense bit index [param peer_id] was assigned in the committed matrix, the index every [method interest_bit_admits] and [method interest_explain_bit] call takes. Answers [code]-1[/code] for a peer the matrix never registered, including one that has since disconnected.

method.name: interest_peer_connected
method.description: Handles [signal peer_connected] for the interest band: admits [param peer_id] into [method interest_known_peers], resyncs the live-peer set, and schedules the [Callable] installed by [method set_interest_compat_refresh] before requesting a flush through [method interest_request_flush]. A joining peer reads the committed matrix only after this has run, so a game never calls it directly.

method.name: interest_peer_disconnected
method.description: Handles [signal peer_disconnected] for the interest band: forgets [param peer_id]'s pending awareness edges and leave bookkeeping, resyncs the live-peer set, then requests a flush through [method interest_request_flush] so the committed matrix stops naming a peer that is gone.

method.name: interest_reapply_perception
method.description: Re-derives [param entity]'s local presentation from scratch: if the local peer already holds a perception verdict for it, that verdict is cleared and restored first, then the perception policies are resolved again as if the entity had just become a candidate. A perception policy change on an already-hidden entity calls this so the new policy's hide or custom behavior takes over rather than layering on top of the old one.

method.name: interest_receive_awareness
method.description: Decodes [param payload] as a reliable batch of awareness edges and applies each once its [NetwEntity]'s route is live. A batch is refused whole when [param sender] is not [constant MultiplayerPeer.TARGET_PEER_SERVER]; a row within it is refused individually when it is not the five typed fields a well-formed edge carries, when its route or layer id is empty, or when a layer-scoped row carries an observer peer or an observer-scoped row carries none. An entering edge waits for its route to become live, so it never applies against an entity that has not arrived yet; an exiting edge for a route that is not live is dropped rather than held, because a route this peer no longer holds has nothing left to retract.

method.name: interest_recompute
method.description: Folds every layer's current membership and viewer state into a pending delta against the committed matrix, without publishing it: readers keep seeing the previous matrix until [method interest_commit] swaps it in. A peer that holds no committed matrix of its own discards any pending delta here and reports success without folding anything, so both roles can drive the same flush.

method.name: interest_request_flush
method.description: Schedules the installed interest flush under [method interest_flush_key]. Every write that can change a committed visibility row goes through here, so the recompute is a property of the write rather than of whichever interface happened to make it. With no layer driver installed the settle is the only thing that recomputes visibility at all, which is why a release that skipped this would leave a departed peer still admitted and still fed. With no flush installed by [method set_interest_flush] this reports and schedules nothing, because a silently dropped flush is indistinguishable from a flush that had nothing to do. It is not counted: the verdict ledger behind [method verdict_total] partitions remote-input verdicts, and a session that never installed its flush is a defect in the caller rather than something a peer did.

method.name: interest_resolved_layer_ids
method.description: The [StringName] ids of every layer [param entity] currently belongs to, sorted for stable iteration. On the server this reads the committed membership directly; off the server, when the entity carries no local membership yet, it falls back to the labels declared on the local [member NetwEntity.interest] facet.

method.name: interest_session_ended
method.description: Handles [signal session_ended] for the interest band by deferring the session's interest state to the next idle frame rather than clearing it inline. The same emission drives a despawn cascade that must drain the entities it names before the layer, awareness, and leave state naming those entities is emptied, and clearing inline would race that cascade.

method.name: interest_set_entity_intent
method.description: Replaces the peers [param entity] is admitted to with [param admitted] in one write, adopts [param entity] into the liveness and lifecycle tracking that clears its interest state when it exits the tree, and requests an interest flush so the new intent is committed. A synchronizer's per-peer visibility decision calls this once per refresh with the full admitted set, not incrementally.

method.name: interest_shared_entities
method.description: Every other live [NetwEntity] that shares a layer with [param entity], excluding [param entity] itself and ordered by [member NetwEntity.entity_id]. An empty [param layer_id] widens the search to every layer [param entity] resolves through [method interest_resolved_layer_ids]; a non-empty one that [param entity] does not itself belong to answers no entities. On the server this walks the committed co-membership roster; off the server, when that roster is empty, it falls back to scanning this peer's own live entities and keeping those whose declared labels intersect the wanted set.

method.name: interest_sync_record
method.description: Writes one entity's place in the interest engine: its parent link and its deterministic (depth, route) order. Ancestors are written first, because a clamp that read a parent the engine has not heard of would leave the child unspawnable until something else happened to touch the parent. The chain climbs from each entity's owner to the nearest record above it, and stops at a key it has already seen, so a parent link that closes on itself costs one pass rather than the process. An entity with no route of its own is ordered by a fallback route the session mints, since the route tiebreak has to be total before there is a route.

method.name: interest_sync_scene_membership
method.description: Reconciles [param entity]'s scene layer roster with its current ancestry: resolves the scene [param entity]'s owner sits in, removes the entity from whatever scene layer it was previously counted in, and adds it to the current one. This only keeps the roster accurate for scene-scoped queries; visibility itself is already governed by the ancestry clamp on the parent, independent of this membership. [br][br][b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: interest_wire_admits
method.description: Whether traffic for [param entity] may reach [param peer_id], short-circuiting [code]true[/code] for [constant MultiplayerPeer.TARGET_PEER_SERVER] because server authority always knows every entity it holds. Every other peer falls through to [method interest_participant_sees]. Replication and spawn gating call this rather than [method interest_participant_sees], because a wire gate that hid the server's own entities from itself would stall authority rather than protect it.

method.name: layer_close
method.description: Releases [param layer]'s name and its view together, so nothing else answers for either afterward. Reopening the same name with [method layer_open] mints a fresh handle rather than reusing [param layer], because a closed handle is never reused.

method.name: layer_forget_all
method.description: Releases every open layer's name and view, and frees every handle [method layer_open] has minted.

method.name: layer_name_of
method.description: The name [param layer] was opened under, or an empty [StringName] when [param layer] names no open layer.

method.name: layer_named
method.description: The handle already open under [param name], or an invalid [RID] when nothing has opened [param name] yet. Unlike [method layer_open], this never builds a view: it only reads the book of names already open.

method.name: layer_open
method.description: Opens the interest layer named [param name], building its view through the installed factory and handing back the handle that names it from then on. Idempotent by name: a second ask for a name already open answers the first handle and builds no second view. Refuses an empty [param name] and a call with no factory installed, in both cases answering an invalid [RID] rather than a handle nothing backs. [codeblock] core.set_layer_factory(interest.layer) var handle := core.layer_open(&"nearby") var view := core.layer_view(handle) [/codeblock]

method.name: layer_view
method.description: The view [param layer] names, read straight from the views book that is the single source of truth for whether [param layer] is live. Answers null when [param layer] names no open layer.

method.name: live_scenes
method.description: Every scene the session holds live, in the order they entered. It answers the book rather than the tree, so a scene whose node has already left still appears here until its exit is recorded. A caller that means "live and mounted" tests for the node itself, because the two questions differ for exactly the span between a node leaving and its exit landing, and collapsing them here would pick one answer for everybody.

method.name: liveness_adopt
method.description: Introduces [param wrapper] to this session, so the index answers for it, and hands back the handle it already carries. Idempotent, and it never mints: the handle is the wrapper's own, held since it was constructed.

method.name: liveness_adopt_route
method.description: Gives [param route] to [param wrapper], adopting the record the route already stands for when it stands for a dead one. A route names one entity across every life it has, so a re-admission takes the standing handle rather than minting a second name for it, and the record comes back live one epoch higher. Answers [constant @GlobalScope.OK] when the caller now owes the announcement, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS] when [param wrapper] was already standing on a live route and owes nothing, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] when the route belongs to another entity or already carries an identity this session holds. The announcement is [method liveness_publish_live], separately, because the caller wires the wrapper's own node signals in between and a listener must not learn the route is live before those are standing.

method.name: liveness_allocate_route
method.description: The route [param wrapper] stands on, reserving and binding one when it stands on none. Two asks about one entity answer the same route.

method.name: liveness_bind
method.description: Binds [param wrapper] to [param route] in the record plane and the index at once. Answers [code]false[/code] when the plane refused, and changes nothing when it does, so a caller never wires a route the plane does not hold. Announcing is [method liveness_publish_live], separately, because the caller wires the wrapper's own node signals in between and a listener must not learn the route is live before those are standing.

method.name: liveness_bind_route
method.description: Gives [param route] to [param wrapper] and announces it live, reading the wrapper's own [NetwEntityRecord] and owner rather than being handed them. The order inside is the contract: the owner's [signal Node.tree_exiting] and the wrapper's despawn hook stand BEFORE [method liveness_publish_live], because a listener must not learn a route is live while the signals that will retire it are unconnected.

method.name: liveness_bind_routes_data
method.description: Binds every route in [param routes] as a live entity with no wrapper and no node, which is the identity a replicated table row is. It emits no [signal entity_live], because a wave of two thousand rows carries no wrapper a listener could reach through. A caller parked on [method NetwMultiplayer.when_live] is still answered.

method.name: liveness_clear_session
method.description: Empties the record plane and the wrapper index between sessions. Wrappers keep their handles, which outlive every session that adopts one.

method.name: liveness_linger
method.description: Moves [param entity] to [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LINGERING] and emits [signal entity_lingering].

method.name: liveness_live_entities
method.description: Every wrapper this peer currently holds a [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LIVE] route for, ordered by route so two calls in one frame agree. This is the peer's own visible set and nothing more: a route is here only because this peer was sent the spawn.

method.name: liveness_node_of
method.description: The root [Node] [param route] names, or [code]null[/code] once the tree has freed it.

method.name: liveness_owner_despawning
method.description: Moves a lingering teardown's route to [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LINGERING]. A despawn without linger changes nothing here, because its route dies at the owner's tree exit instead.

method.name: liveness_owner_exiting
method.description: Resolves an owner leaving the tree. A move in flight is not a teardown, so a [member NetwEntity.reparenting] entity is left alone. A route the spawn ledger tracks resolves at the next settle through [method liveness_resolve_tracked_exit] instead, so a remove-then-add reparent before that pump never kills the route.

method.name: liveness_pending_live_count
method.description: How many parked callbacks are still waiting for a binding, the liveness backlog [InterestMonitor] surfaces.

method.name: liveness_poll
method.description: Advances the record plane's frame counter and expires whatever aged out, warning for each route whose last waiter timed out. Pass the tick a configured clock reads, or [code]0[/code] when none is.

method.name: liveness_publish_live
method.description: Announces [param route] live as [signal entity_live], resolving the wrapper from the index itself. It takes only the route, because the session is what knows which wrapper that route names and a caller passing one could pass a different one than the index holds.

method.name: liveness_reserve_route
method.description: Advances the route counter and answers what it handed out, binding nothing to it. Allocation is monotonic and a route is never reused, tombstone included, so a name this returns can only ever mean the entity that claims it.

method.name: liveness_resolve_tracked_exit
method.description: The settled half of the reparent grace: a tracked owner back inside the tree was reparented, and anything else is a real despawn. A [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LINGERING] route resolves here too, so a linger-then-free still reaches [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_DEAD].

method.name: liveness_retire
method.description: Retires [param route]: the state move to [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_DEAD], the waiter drop, the index move from live to retired, and [signal entity_dead]. One act, because the announcement carries a route whose wrapper a listener must be able to resolve exactly as it will be for the rest of the cycle. It clears [member local_player] only when the entity DYING is the one representing this peer, asked by identity rather than by route: a scene change binds the replacement before retiring the original, so a route-keyed test drops a local player that had already moved on.

method.name: liveness_route_of
method.description: The route bound to [param wrapper], or [code]0[/code].

method.name: liveness_route_state
method.description: The [enum NetwLivenessCore.State] of [param route].

method.name: liveness_settle_local_player
method.description: Settles which entity represents this peer, now that [param route] is live. Separate from [method liveness_publish_live] because a listener on the live edge reads [member local_player] while the cascade runs, so the answer changes at the point in that cascade where it always has. It takes only the route and reads the entity's own [NetwEntityRecord], so a caller cannot name a local player the session did not choose. A session with no transport represents nobody.

method.name: liveness_state_of
method.description: The [enum NetwLivenessCore.State] of [param wrapper], or [constant NetwLivenessCore.STATE_UNKNOWN] for a wrapper carrying no record.

method.name: liveness_tombstone_routes_data
method.description: Tombstones every route in [param routes] without emitting [signal entity_dead], the death edge of [method liveness_bind_routes_data]. A tombstoned route is never reissued, which is what lets a receiver drop a row for it rather than resurrect one.

method.name: liveness_transition_dead
method.description: Retires [param route] with its wrapper's node and despawn hooks taken down first, so the retirement announcement cannot reach the handler that caused it.

method.name: liveness_when_live
method.description: Parks [param callback] on [param route] until it goes live, running it at once when the route already is. [param deadline] is a plain integer and [param on_clock] names which counter it is measured against, because the tick clock is a session service a rig may never configure. [method NetwMultiplayer.when_live] is the door that settles both from a timeout in ticks.

method.name: next_send_seq
method.description: The next outbound sequence for [param peer], wrapped at 16 bits. Taking it advances the book, so two datagrams to one peer can never share a stamp.

method.name: note_echoed_seq
method.description: Records that [param seq] has been echoed back to [param peer].

method.name: note_inbound_seq
method.description: Whether [param seq] was fresher than what this session already held for [param peer]. A reordered datagram is dropped rather than recorded.

method.name: note_peer_ack
method.description: Whether [param ack] advanced [param peer]'s confirmed baseline. A stalled echo from a silent peer holds its baseline rather than corrupting it, and the false answer is what tells a caller not to promote anything.

method.name: overrides_seam
method.description: Whether [param script] REDECLARES [param seam] somewhere between itself and [param base_name], rather than merely inheriting it. A method list carries inherited entries too, so only the count separates the two. Resolved once per seam, because a script's method table cannot change for a live session.

method.name: participant_admit
method.description: Marks [param peer]'s roster row as admitted, answering whether this call is what admitted it. A peer holding no row cannot be admitted, because admission is a fact about a row rather than a second book that could name a peer the roster does not. Admission and announcement are two edges, not one: this is the moment the session accepted the join, while [method participant_publish_joined] is the moment it told everyone. The gap between them is where the join handler runs, so a listener inside that gap reads an admitted participant here and reads [signal local_participant_joined] as not yet fired. A row that is forgotten or cleared takes its admission with it, so admission never outlives the row it describes.

method.name: participant_admitted_all
method.description: Every admitted row, in peer order so two reads in one frame agree. [method participant_all] answers the whole roster instead, the un-joined observers included.

method.name: participant_admitted_local
method.description: This peer's admitted row, or [code]null[/code]. The session decides for itself which peer is this one, so a caller never passes an id it would have to read from somewhere else and could read at the wrong moment. This answers from [method participant_admit] onward, which is earlier than [signal local_participant_joined] fires.

method.name: participant_admitted_of
method.description: [param peer]'s row once it is admitted, or [code]null[/code]. A connected peer that has not joined holds a row that [method participant_of] answers and this one does not.

method.name: participant_adopt
method.description: Adopts [param participant] as [param peer]'s roster row. A peer already holding one keeps it, so two asks answer the same object rather than two. The row is minted by the caller and held here, for the same reason the wrapper index holds a reference: this is what keeps it alive.

method.name: participant_all
method.description: Every roster row, un-joined observers included, in peer order so two reads in one frame agree.

method.name: participant_clear
method.description: Drops every row. Session teardown, so a same-session re-host starts empty.

method.name: participant_ensure
method.description: Answers the [NetwParticipant] for [param peer], minting it on the first ask and answering the same object on every later one. The session mints the row rather than a caller handing one in, because two callers minting for one peer would be two objects a game could hold and compare unequal. Minting is idempotent and carries no join: a row exists from the moment a peer is asked about, and [member NetwParticipant.join] stays null until the join is accepted.

method.name: participant_forget
method.description: Drops [param peer]'s row.

method.name: participant_has
method.description: Whether [param peer] holds a row.

method.name: participant_identity
method.description: The validated [NetwIdentity] for [param peer], or [code]null[/code]. Backs [member NetwParticipant.identity] through the reader installed by [method set_identity_reader].

method.name: participant_leave_seat
method.description: Empties [param peer]'s seat, but only when [param scene] is the one it currently holds. A move reassigns the seat before the scene it left releases it, so a release naming the older scene must not evict the participant from the newer one. The write alone, announcing nothing: [method participant_seat_clear] is the verb that also tells the row.

method.name: participant_move_seat
method.description: Moves [param peer] into [param scene] as one act: the seat is reassigned, the scene it left releases its admission boundary, and [param scene] admits it. Answers whether the seat moved, which is the whole of the decision. A [param peer] the roster never opened, a [param scene] naming no live container, and a [param peer] already seated in [param scene] all answer [code]false[/code] and touch no boundary. The order is what makes the move a move rather than a release followed by an admission. The seat is reassigned first, so by the time the older scene releases the peer, the seat no longer names it and [method scene_notify_released] refuses: a moved peer is never told it was released, because it is being told where it went by the seat edge instead, and a release notice would have it present a scene it has already left. [method participant_seat_move] is the seat write and its announcement alone, without either boundary. This is the verb that also carries the admission across, and is what every mover wants. The recompute both boundary writes request is queued rather than run, so a caller that needs the committed matrix before it returns flushes once after this rather than twice inside it.

method.name: participant_of
method.description: [param peer]'s roster row, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: participant_publish_joined
method.description: Announces [param peer]'s row as joined, and binds it as the local participant when that peer is this one, before the announcement, so a listener that reacts by changing scene has its change published rather than dropped. It takes only the peer, because the session holds the row and decides for itself whether that peer is this one: the local announcement has to precede the general one, and a caller deciding which to send could send them in either order or send only one.

method.name: participant_seat
method.description: The scene identity [param peer]'s participant is seated in, or an invalid [RID] when it holds no seat.

method.name: participant_seat_clear
method.description: [method participant_leave_seat] followed by the announcement it owes, answering whether the seat emptied. The row's [code]scene_changed[/code] signal is emitted with the handle of the seat it held and [code]null[/code], and only when the seat actually emptied, so a release naming a scene the participant no longer holds announces nothing. This is the verb a caller uses. [method participant_leave_seat] is the silent write underneath it, and a caller that takes it announces nothing, which strands every listener on [signal local_scene_changed].

method.name: participant_seat_move
method.description: [method participant_take_seat] followed by the announcement it owes, answering whether the seat changed. The row's [code]scene_changed[/code] signal is emitted with the handles of the seat left and the seat taken, and only when the seat actually changed, so a re-seat into the scene already held announces nothing. The [code]from[/code] handle is read from the record book by [method scene_handle_of] rather than from whichever node stands in for the scene, so a move away from a scene whose container has already been freed still names what was left. This is the verb a caller uses. [method participant_take_seat] is the silent write underneath it, and a caller that takes it announces nothing, which strands every listener on [signal local_scene_changed].

method.name: participant_seated_in
method.description: Every peer seated in [param scene], in peer order.

method.name: participant_take_seat
method.description: Seats [param peer] in [param scene], answering whether the seat changed. The write alone, announcing nothing: [method participant_seat_move] is the verb that also tells the row, and is what a caller wants unless it is deliberately reseating a participant behind every listener's back.

method.name: peer_ack
method.description: The freshest sequence [param peer] has confirmed holding, or [code]-1[/code] when it has confirmed nothing. Negative rather than zero, because zero is a sequence a peer can genuinely have acked.

method.name: peers_owed_echo
method.description: Every peer this session holds a fresher inbound sequence for than it has echoed back. Answering it is the whole of the standalone-ack decision that does not depend on a transport.

method.name: poll_delta
method.description: Seconds since the previous poll, and zero on a session's first poll because there is no earlier one to measure against. Reading it MARKS this poll, so a second reader in the same frame is answered zero. [param now_usec] is the caller's reading of the wall clock, handed down rather than taken here.

method.name: presents_as_listen_host
method.description: Whether this peer either already holds [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER] or authors it as its intent, through [method authored_desired_role]. Either alone is enough, because the two readings are true at different times: the authored intent is what a session about to host answers before it has resolved a role, and the resolved role is what it answers afterwards, including when the configuration was re-authored to something else in between.

method.name: property_path
method.description: [param property] on [param source], relative to [param base]. Empty when either node is gone, because falling through would answer a bare property name that writes whichever node the reader happened to hold. A node addresses itself as [code]"."[/code], so a property on the base is a valid self-address.

method.name: receive_header
method.description: Reads one inbound datagram's header, announcing and counting as it goes. A packet that is not Networked framing is emitted as [signal peer_packet] rather than answered about, because the session is the only thing that can tell the application's traffic from its own. Everything the session does own is counted into [member received_packets] and [member received_bytes], body bytes only, so two peers' throughput is comparable. A datagram of ours that cannot be read is neither announced nor counted. It answers the header rather than only the kind so a caller drives the rest from one read. The read is a three-way answer, and a watched session sees all three ways it can go: a datagram of ours leaves a [code]DATAGRAM_RECEIVED[/code] row, one of ours that cannot be read leaves a [code]DATAGRAM_MALFORMED[/code] row, and the application's own traffic leaves neither because it was never ours to report.

method.name: relative_path
method.description: A path from [param source] to [param target], empty when either is gone. The one spelling, so a path built for a wire address and one built for a property binding cannot come to differ.

method.name: reset_interest
method.description: Drops every interest layer's roster and viewer set.

method.name: scene_activate
method.description: Brings [param destination] up if it is not already live and forces its content root to process, answering the container it settled on or [code]null[/code] when nothing could be activated. It never announces: a caller that publishes an activation signal emits it for the node this answers, once, which is what keeps one activation from being announced twice. [param destination] is partitioned by [method NetwSceneCore.destination_kind]. A name defers wholly to [method scene_activate_named]. A file-backed [PackedScene] reuses the live container its stem answers for, and spawns from the packed scene's own path when none is live. An in-memory [PackedScene] is refused, because a peer receiving the spawn has no path to load it from, and a [Node] is refused too, because an already-mounted node is not something to activate. [codeblock] DESTINATION_NAME -> scene_activate_named(name) DESTINATION_PACKED -> the live container, else a spawn DESTINATION_PACKED_UNPATHED -> refused DESTINATION_NODE -> refused DESTINATION_NONE -> refused [/codeblock]

method.name: scene_activate_named
method.description: Ensures a live scene carries [param stem] and forces its content root to process, answering that container or [code]null[/code] when the stem could not be brought up. A stem already live is returned as it stands. Otherwise the declaration decides how it is built: a session that declared a [member NetwSceneConfig.level_spawn_function] spawns through [method scene_spawn] with the stem's declared spawn data, and a session that declared none spawns through [method scene_spawn_declared], which reads the stem's declared path. The container is re-read after the spawn rather than taken from it, so a constructor that mounted nothing answers [code]null[/code] rather than a half-built scene. A content-less container is activated without forcing anything, because a pure admission boundary has no content root to process.

method.name: scene_admit
method.description: Admits [param peer] to [param scene], answering [constant @GlobalScope.OK] only once the admission has taken. The verb over [method scene_admit_peer]'s raw write: it refuses peer zero, refuses a scene whose node is gone, and re-reads [method scene_admits] afterwards rather than trusting the write, so a caller is told what actually happened instead of what was attempted. It does NOT flush interest. The flush runs layer drivers, which are the authoring tier's, so the door that admits is here and the door that recomputes stays with whoever owns the drivers. [b][br][br]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_admit_peer
method.description: Adds [param peer] as a viewer of [param scene]'s admission boundary and requests the flush that recomputes what that admission reveals. Answers whether the boundary changed, so an admission that was already held reports [code]false[/code] and no caller can mistake a repeat for a new arrival. The boundary is minted by the write itself, because a scene armed this frame carries no layer until something admits somebody to it, and a lookup that could not create one would silently drop every admission a scene change makes. Admission is one interest edge rather than an enrolment: every entity the scene encloses inherits it through the parent clamp. A peer of [code]0[/code] and a [param scene] that names no boundary admit nobody. A boundary that changed reports the arrival to [method set_scene_participant_edge], after the flush is requested, so every path that admits somebody reports it without each caller remembering to.

method.name: scene_admits
method.description: Whether [param scene] currently admits [param peer], read from the scene's interest layer rather than from any book of its own, so an admission revoked by the layer is not still reported here.

method.name: scene_answer_when_settled
method.description: Answers [param peer]'s [param request_id] with [param operation]'s settle code, at the moment that operation settles. Subscribing rather than awaiting is what lets a request be answered from a caller that has no coroutine: an [param operation] already settled is answered now, and a pending one is answered on its own [signal NetwPromise.settled] edge, exactly once. A null [param operation] is answered [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] rather than dropped, because a request left unanswered costs the requester its whole deadline to learn the same thing. The code sent is [member NetwPromise.code], so an operation that resolved reports [constant @GlobalScope.OK] and one that rejected reports why.

method.name: scene_build_container
method.description: The orphan container one scene mounts under, built for the isolation it declared. A hosting peer isolates an [param own_world] scene in a [SubViewport] with its own 3D world and no render target, and every other case is a plain [Node], because only the host simulates. Neither carries a script: a scene is its entity record, not a node class. The container is named [code]Scene[/code] and carries [method scene_container_meta], so a walk with no session to ask can still find one. The caller owns it and parents it.

method.name: scene_capture_verdict
method.description: What this peer does with a marked scene root that entered the tree through the engine's own [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_file] rather than through a session verb, as one of [enum NetwSceneCore.Capture]. Every input the verdict turns on is read here rather than passed in, because they are all readings of this session: whether [param path] names a saved file at all, whether this peer is authority, the reach set by [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_set_request_reach], whether any scene is already live, whether authority is a listen host with an admitted local participant, and whether the seat that participant holds is a world of its own. A caller that gathered them itself would be re-deriving the session's own state at the one door where a disagreement strands the peer outside every scene. The rule those readings feed is [method NetwSceneCore.native_entry_verdict], which decides and never reads.

method.name: scene_constructor_id
method.description: The spawn-registry id the session's own scene constructor is registered under, so a session with no [MultiplayerSceneManager] still reconstructs a scene wrapper on every peer. One spelling, read from here rather than written a second time, because the registrar and [method scene_spawn] name it independently and a mismatch is a spawn that silently reconstructs nothing.

method.name: scene_container
method.description: The container node the live scene named [param stem] is mounted under, or [code]null[/code] when no live scene carries that stem. It is the node tier of [method scene_named]: a caller that looked a scene up by name and means to mount, free or reparent it wants the node rather than the [RID].

method.name: scene_container_meta
method.description: The metadata key [method scene_build_container] stamps a container with. One spelling, read from here rather than written a second time, because the walk that reads it runs off-session where nothing else identifies a container.

method.name: scene_containing
method.description: The container of the scene [param node] sits inside, or [code]null[/code] when nothing on its ancestor chain is a live scene. The walk climbs from [param node] and stops at the first ancestor that both the scene book holds live and [method wrapper_owner] answers with, which is what makes it answer with the node the session MOUNTED rather than with a level root that merely declares a scene of its own. That distinction matters because the mounted container is what every reparent and free targets.

method.name: scene_declared
method.description: Whether [param entity] declares itself a scene. An entity the session never bound answers [code]false[/code] rather than refusing, because asking about a stranger is an ordinary question.

method.name: scene_despawn
method.description: Takes down the live scene whose stem is the name of [param scene]'s content root. It resolves that stem from [param scene]'s first child, finds the live container the scene book answers for it, and splits on [param drain_pumps]. At zero or less, the container leaves the tree and is freed immediately. At a positive count, the container stays mounted and [method NetwSceneCore.scene_retire] opens its drain window instead, so frames already in flight still have somewhere to land, and the installed scene-refresh callable is scheduled on the settle queue to re-read the peer's current scene once the retirement has landed. Refuses with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when [param scene] has no node, when it holds no content root to name a stem, and when no live scene answers to that stem. Nothing is taken down on a refusal.

method.name: scene_destination_kind
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwSceneCore.destination_kind], answering the same partition as one [enum SceneDestination]. The record plane is registered internally, so this and the other [code]scene_*[/code] statics here are the whole of its scripted reach.

method.name: scene_destroy
method.description: Unparents and frees the live container named [param stem] on the spot, answering whether one was found. No drain window and no settle pass: this is the take-down for a scene whose in-flight frames are not worth keeping addressable, and [method scene_retire_named] is the one that keeps them so. A stem no live scene carries answers [code]false[/code] silently, because destroying what is already gone is the caller's intended end state.

method.name: scene_entities_under
method.description: Every entity [param scene] encloses, excluding itself. The walk descends through nodes that own no record, so a plain node between a scene and its members hides nobody, and it stops at a nested declared scene, so a scene reports its own members and never the members of a scene it merely contains. That stop is what makes membership ancestry rather than containment.

method.name: scene_entity_node
method.description: The node [param entity] is bound to, or [code]null[/code]. The reachability every scene verb tests before it writes anything.

method.name: scene_existing_destination
method.description: The container an ALREADY LIVE destination stands for, or [code]null[/code] when nothing live matches. It never activates anything, so a caller can ask whether a destination is already up before deciding to spawn it. [param destination] is partitioned by [method NetwSceneCore.destination_kind]. A [Node] answers only while the scene book holds it live, a name and a file-backed [PackedScene] both resolve through [method scene_container], and anything else answers [code]null[/code]. [codeblock] DESTINATION_NODE -> the node itself, while it is live DESTINATION_NAME -> scene_container(name) DESTINATION_PACKED -> scene_container(packed stem) DESTINATION_PACKED_UNPATHED -> scene_container(packed stem) DESTINATION_NONE -> null [/codeblock]

method.name: scene_forget
method.description: Drops [param container]'s scene from the live book and schedules the installed scene refresh, so a peer whose current scene just left re-reads what it is presenting once the edge has settled. It frees nothing: the node is already leaving, and this is the record plane catching up with it.

method.name: scene_freeze
method.description: Disables processing on the content root of the live scene named [param stem], answering whether one was found to disable. The container itself keeps processing, because it is the admission boundary and its replication must survive its level being stopped. A stem with no live scene and a live scene with no content root both answer [code]false[/code].

method.name: scene_handle_of
method.description: The scene facet [param entity] publishes itself through, or [code]null[/code] for an entity this session holds no record for. It is the record's own facet ([constant NetwEntityRecord.PART_SCENE]) rather than a copy the session was handed, because the handle IS the scene's public identity and two would be two scenes.

method.name: scene_hosts_isolated_world
method.description: Whether any live scene is mounted in a container that owns its own world, which is the only thing a listen-server host has left to draw. A host whose scenes all share the session's world renders like a client and needs no host presentation view at all. It is read off the CONTAINER rather than off the record, because a container hosting its own world IS the [SubViewport] holding it, and [method scene_build_container] is the one place that decides which containers are built that way.

method.name: scene_install_level
method.description: Mounts [param level] as [param container]'s only child and renames the container after it, which is what makes a container's first child its content root. Either being gone installs nothing rather than half-mounting.

method.name: scene_layer_id
method.description: The layer id naming [param scene]'s admission boundary, or empty when its container holds no content root. It is the content root's name and, once the scene has one, its route, because a stem alone collides across two live scenes built from the same content. A scene armed this frame has no route yet and is keyed by the stem alone until one lands. Distinct from [method scene_stem], which prefers a declared label. A caller asking what a scene is CALLED and a caller asking which layer admits it are not asking the same question.

method.name: scene_layer_view
method.description: The view of the layer that admits [param scene], or [code]null[/code] when the scene names no boundary or none is open for it yet. This is [method scene_layer_id] and the lookup installed by [method set_layer_lookup] taken as one act, because every caller that wanted the id wanted the layer, and spelling the composition twice is two chances to key a lookup on a stem that has since gained a route. It never mints. A scene that nobody has admitted anybody to has no layer, and answering [code]null[/code] is the difference between "nobody is admitted here" and "this boundary exists and is empty". [method scene_admit_peer] is the write that mints one.

method.name: scene_level_of
method.description: The content root [param container] holds, which is its only child, or [code]null[/code] when it holds none. It is the read half of [method scene_install_level]: a container's first child is its content root because that is the one this mounts there. A scene with no content root is a pure admission boundary rather than a broken scene, so answering [code]null[/code] is an answer and not a failure. It is also what names the scene's stem, which is why [method scene_despawn] resolves a stem through here.

method.name: scene_mark_of
