method.description: What [param script] declares about how a session may reach the scene it roots, as a [NetwSceneMark]. Always answers a record. A null [param script], a script that declares nothing, and a session with no reader installed all read as every field at its default, so a door reads facts off the record instead of branching on absence. The reading is delegated to the [Callable] installed by [method set_scene_mark_reader], because a mark is authored against a [Script] and only the script tier can key by one.

method.name: scene_move_entity
method.description: Moves [param entity] into the scene [param destination] names, answering the [NetwPromise] that move settles through. It always answers a promise. A move that cannot start, because either handle names no live node or no carry is installed, is rejected [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] rather than dropped, so a caller subscribes to one thing whatever the outcome. The reparent itself is delegated to the [Callable] installed by [method set_scene_carry_move], because the body has to be off the physics server's overlap lists before it moves and back on them after, which is a window counted in physics frames rather than in session ticks. What stays here is the pair of handles, the promise, and the reachability that decides whether the carry is worth entering at all. [param opts] is a [NetwReparentOpts] or [code]null[/code]. One carrying no [member NetwReparentOpts.reason] is stamped with [method scene_move_reason] before the carry sees it, so a move is always attributable in a reparent record even when its caller only wanted a destination. Passing [code]null[/code] stays null and takes the entity plane's own defaults.

method.name: scene_move_participants
method.description: Moves every peer in [param peers] into [param scene] through [method participant_move_seat], answering the [NetwGroupPromise] that reports the arrivals. The batch expects exactly [param peers], including a peer the move refuses, because a caller asked for that peer and is owed an answer about it either way. What refusal costs is the seat, not the report. The report is scheduled rather than made, and it is what settles the group. A caller cannot subscribe to a promise it has not been handed yet, so a group settled before this returns is a group whose [signal NetwGroupPromise.completed_single] nobody can hear. Draining the settle queue is what delivers it, and it is delivered from the session's own pump rather than from a frame, so a session with no tree reports its arrivals on the same schedule a rendered one does. It is scheduled unkeyed, so two moves in one cascade settle as two groups. A shared key would coalesce them and strand the first caller on a promise that never settles. A group nobody could move, [param peers] empty most of all, still settles at that same drain: the last arrival is what settles every other group, and here there is no arrival to be last. [codeblock] var batch := core.scene_move_participants(arena, PackedInt32Array([7, 9])) batch.completed_single.connect(greet) core.settle_drain() [/codeblock]

method.name: scene_move_reason
method.description: The [member NetwReparentOpts.reason] a scene move records when its caller named none. A scene move and a bare reparent reach the same entity plane, so without this every move authored as "put this entity in that scene" would land in the record indistinguishable from a reparent authored for any other purpose. Reading it here rather than spelling the string at each door is what keeps the two readings equal.

method.name: scene_move_verdict
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwSceneCore.move_verdict], answering the same three arms as one [enum SceneMove].

method.name: scene_named
method.description: A live scene whose stem is [param stem], or an invalid [RID]. Stems are not unique, so this answers "an instance of this stem" rather than "the one". Use [method scenes_named] wherever the difference between an instance and every one of them can change the outcome.

method.name: scene_native_change_strands
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwSceneCore.native_change_strands].

method.name: scene_notify_released
method.description: Tells [param peer], on its own side, that it no longer belongs to [param scene], answering whether anything was sent or delivered. A client learns its membership from awareness of the scene entity, and awareness that goes away cannot say why, so the release is a frame rather than something the peer works out. The frame carries [method scene_layer_id], which is the same name the boundary is keyed by. It is guarded by [method participant_seat]: a peer that does not currently sit in [param scene] is told nothing, because a release it never held would tear down the seat it does hold. That guard is why this runs before [method scene_release_peer] rather than after. A [param peer] that is this peer is delivered straight to the channel's own protocol handler instead of being sent, so a listen-server host releasing itself takes the same path as the client it also is.

method.name: scene_observe
method.description: Registers [param callback] for one scene [param event] on [param scene]. An invalid [param scene] or an unset [param callback] registers nothing, and registering the same [param callback] twice stores it once, so an edge is heard once. [param event] is a raw ordinal mirroring the [code]NetwMultiplayer.SceneEvent[/code] enum, which stays the one published spelling. Plural where a layer monitor is singular, because several unrelated observers legitimately watch one scene while a layer's monitor is the session's own. The registration names the scene [RID] rather than a node, so it survives whichever node currently stands in for that scene. [b]An observer retires itself by answering [code]true[/code][/b], and one answering anything else, including nothing, is kept. This is the only way to drop one registration when several share a base [Callable]: [method scene_unobserve] matches with [code]==[/code], and a bound [Callable] compares equal on its base and its bind [i]count[/i] rather than on the values bound, so a relay that binds its subscriber cannot be told apart from its own sibling. Answering the retirement is identity-free, which is what makes it exact. An observer whose object has been freed is dropped on the next dispatch without being called, so retiring is for a live observer that has decided it is finished.

method.name: scene_owns_its_world
method.description: Whether [param scene]'s entity record declares [constant NetwSceneCore.ISOLATION_OWN_WORLD], which is the fact the session reads when it warns that two levels are sharing one physics space. It answers off [member NetwEntity.scene_isolation], so it is the DECLARED reading rather than the mounted one. A caller asking what is actually drawn asks [method scene_hosts_isolated_world] instead, which reads the container.

method.name: scene_packed_at
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwSceneCore.packed_at].

method.name: scene_packed_root_script
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwSceneCore.packed_root_script].

method.name: scene_packed_stem
method.description: The stem [param packed] would enter the live book under, which is the name of its content root. Empty for a null or contentless scene. It is deliberately NOT the resource path's file name. A scene file is named in snake_case and its root node in PascalCase by convention, so the two disagree for almost every scene, and a lookup keyed on the file name finds nothing and silently spawns a duplicate.

method.name: scene_peers
method.description: Every peer [param scene]'s admission boundary currently admits, empty for a scene that names no boundary. It reads the viewers the boundary holds rather than any enrolment book, so it answers the same fact [method scene_admit_peer] wrote and [method scene_release_peer] cleared, and a scene with no layer open answers empty rather than reporting the whole session. This is the read half of the same boundary those two write. Keeping the composition here is what stops a caller from pairing [method scene_layer_id] with a viewer query of its own and drifting from what admission actually means.

method.name: scene_publish_live
method.description: Records the scene [param route] names as live under [param name] and announces [param container]'s handle as [signal scene_live], in one act: two adjacent calls are two chances to send one without the other. The container is named by the caller rather than walked to here, because [method entity_scene_of] is one stage of a resolution the caller owns, and a second walk would be a second answer. The handle it announces is [method scene_handle_of] on the key you name here, so the announcement cannot publish a handle nobody holds.

method.name: scene_pump_retired
method.description: Advances every retired container's drain window by one pump and frees the ones whose window closed. A clocked session pumps on its ticks and an unclocked one on its polls, which is the cadence each of them actually sends at, so a window counted here counts the chances an in-flight frame had to land. [method NetwSceneCore.pump_retired] decides which windows closed and this frees their nodes, because the record plane holds no nodes.

method.name: scene_receive_result_frame
method.description: Applies a scene-request result frame from [param sender], answering whether it settled the request in flight. A [param sender] other than the server is counted as one [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] verdict before the frame is refused, so a peer forging answers to other peers' requests shows up in [method verdict_total] rather than only in a log line nobody reads. Counting here and refusing in [method NetwSceneCore.receive_result_frame] is one act split by what each half owns: the verdict book is the session's and the request book is the scene plane's.

method.name: scene_release
method.description: Removes [param peer] from [param scene], answering whether anything was done. The telling goes first: [method scene_notify_released] runs while the peer still holds the seat that names what it is being released from, because a client learns membership from awareness of the scene entity and would otherwise keep presenting a scene it no longer belongs to. It does NOT flush interest, for the reason [method scene_admit] does not, and the answer is what tells a caller whether a flush is owed. [b][br][br]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_release_departed
method.description: Releases [param peer] from [param scene] when [param subject] left that scene for good, answering whether the boundary changed. This is the settled half of a player's departure: the exit signal that opens the window cannot tell a free from a reparent, and this is asked once the pump has made the difference readable. A [param mover_live] subject that still resolves to [param scene] through [method entity_scene_of] went nowhere, so nothing is released. A subject that is gone, or that resolves to some other scene, has left, and its seat is released through [method scene_release_peer]. [param mover_live] is asked of the caller rather than read here because the record a departing entity is known by is cleared before its node leaves the tree, so the only holder that can still answer is whoever kept a reference across the window. A peer that is not the server releases nobody, because admission is the server's book.

method.name: scene_release_peer
method.description: Drops [param peer] as a viewer of [param scene]'s admission boundary and requests the flush that recomputes what the release hides. Answers whether the boundary changed, so releasing a peer that was never admitted reports [code]false[/code]. The release and its flush are one act. A release is the half with no eager flush behind it: a peer whose seat is torn down leaves nothing else to recompute the matrix, and a boundary cleared without a flush keeps feeding a departed peer a scene it no longer belongs to. Unlike [method scene_admit_peer] this mints nothing. A scene with no boundary released nobody. A boundary that changed reports the departure to [method set_scene_participant_edge]. It does not tell the released peer, which is [method scene_notify_released] and has to happen while the seat still names what is being released.

method.name: scene_released_seat
method.description: The seat this peer must vacate on a scene-release notice from [param sender], or an invalid [RID] when the notice concerns some other membership. A client learns membership from awareness of the scene entity, which cannot report a release on its own, so the release is sent and this reads it. A notice is honored only from the server, only while this peer holds an admitted participant, and only when the layer id it names is the one [method scene_layer_id] answers for the seat that participant currently holds. The layer id is checked rather than the stem because a session running several instances of one level releases a peer from ONE of them, and a stem would clear the seat in whichever instance the peer happened to be sitting in. Answering the seat rather than clearing it keeps the record's edge with the participant that owns it: this decides which membership the notice named, and the caller is what drops it.

method.name: scene_report_entity_edge
method.description: Dispatches [param subject] crossing the boundary of the scene it resolves to through [method entity_scene_of], as [constant NetwSceneCore.EVENT_ENTITY] carrying [param present], and answers the scene it dispatched against or an invalid [RID] when it dispatched nothing. A [param is_player] subject reports a second time as [constant NetwSceneCore.EVENT_PLAYER], because a player is an entity that also carries a peer rather than a separate population an observer would have to watch twice to see once. A subject that resolves to no scene, or that resolves to ITSELF, reports nothing: a scene container entering its own scene is the walk finding its own starting point, not an arrival anybody asked to hear about. The scene is resolved here rather than remembered by the caller, so an entity reparented between two scenes reports its leave against the one it is still under and its arrival against the one it reached, with nothing handing it over.

method.name: scene_report_moved
method.description: Reports every peer in [param peers] onto [param batch] and settles it. The scheduled half of [method scene_move_participants], which is the only caller that has any business naming it: it runs from the settle drain, one drain after the move it reports. Each peer is resolved with the roster row [method participant_of] answers for it right now, rather than with a row remembered at the move, so a peer the roster dropped between the move and the drain reports as itself with nothing attached instead of handing out a participant the session no longer holds. A [param batch] the arrivals did not settle, an empty [param peers] most of all, is settled here. Resolving the last expected peer is what settles every other group, so a group with nothing expected needs this to be settled at all, and settling it twice is refused by [NetwGroupPromise] rather than guarded here.

method.name: scene_request
method.description: Opens a request on the scene book, stamps it with the book's pending id, and sends that request to server authority on the scene-request channel, as one act. Answers the [NetwPromise] that request settles through. Opening a request supersedes any request this session still has in flight: the previous promise settles [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_SKIP] first, so one peer never has two answers coming. [param destination] is a stem when [param is_path] is false and a resource path when it is true, and the frame carries whichever form the caller used. [param from_capture] records that the request came from a captured native scene entry rather than from a direct ask.

method.name: scene_request_expire
method.description: Settles [param request_id] with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_TIMEOUT], and does nothing when [param request_id] is no longer the request in flight. That stale-id drop is the whole point: a deadline armed for a request already superseded must not answer the request that replaced it. The deadline itself is armed against the engine's wall clock, through the scene tree's own timer, while [method scene_request] and this method are the only acts the request's outcome runs through.

method.name: scene_request_flooded
method.description: Whether [param peer]'s scene requests have passed the rate the session admits joins under, counting one [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_BUSY] verdict when they have. The host carries authority and is never limited. [param now_msec] is handed in rather than read, so the window is a function of its arguments and a case can drive it without a clock. That rate is a window that SLIDES rather than resetting, the same one [method session_receive_join] admits joins under, so a [param peer] requesting steadily under the budget is never refused however long it keeps going, one that spent its budget is admitted again as its oldest request ages out of the span, and a peer that cannot flood the join door cannot reach the same session by this one instead. The table of requesters is bounded, dropping those whose newest request has already aged out rather than remembering every peer that ever asked, and never the [param peer] whose request triggered the drop.

method.name: scene_request_frame_row
method.description: The four fields a scene-request frame from [param sender] carries, in the order [method scene_request] wrote them: request id, whether the destination is a path, the destination, and the request's arguments. An empty [Array] means the frame reaches no policy at all, which is the answer for a peer that is not authority, for a [param sender] past the rate [method scene_request_flooded] admits, and for a payload that is not a four-field row. Decoding here is what keeps the row's shape written once. [method scene_request] is the only writer of this frame, so a reader spelling the four fields somewhere else forks the wire the moment either side gains a field. A fourth field that is not an [Array] is answered as an empty one rather than refusing the whole row, because the arguments are the request handler's to judge and a caller that passed none is not malformed. [param now_msec] is handed in rather than read, for the reason [method scene_request_flooded] states.

method.name: scene_request_open
method.description: Sends the request [method scene_request] sends and arms the deadline that expires it, as one act, answering the same [NetwPromise]. Opening and arming are one act because a request opened without its deadline never settles when authority stays silent, and the id the deadline must name is the one this open just stamped. A caller that did the two steps itself would have to read that id back between them. The wait itself is the engine's wall clock, which this session never touches, so the arming is delegated to the [Callable] installed by [method set_request_deadline_arm]. It receives the request id and [param deadline] in seconds, and is expected to call [method scene_request_expire] with that id once the wait elapses. A [param deadline] of zero or less arms nothing and the request then waits for authority indefinitely, which is also what happens while no arm is installed.

method.name: scene_request_targets
scene_resolve_requested_path
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwSceneCore.resolve_requested_path].

method.name: scene_retire_named
method.description: Drops the live scene named [param stem] from the registry now and leaves its container mounted for [param drain_pumps] more pumps, answering whether one was found. A teardown that must end game logic immediately while keeping stale replication paths resolvable uses this over [method scene_destroy]. The window is counted in pumps because what it holds open is a path for frames still in flight, and the pump is what carries them. A negative count is clamped to zero, which retires with no window rather than freeing: unlike [method scene_despawn] at zero, nothing here frees the container, and [method scene_pump_retired] is what eventually does. The installed scene refresh is scheduled on the settle queue, so a peer presenting the retired scene re-reads what it is presenting once the edge has landed.

method.name: scene_root_script_at
method.description: Forwards to [method NetwSceneCore.scene_root_script_at].

method.name: scene_seat_clear_deferred
method.description: Schedules [method participant_seat_clear] for [param peer] and [param scene] at the next settle, under [method scene_seat_clear_key]. The window exists because a release edge and a reassigning move are the same edge at the moment it fires: a participant moved from one scene to another is released from the first, and clearing the seat there would erase the seat the move just wrote. Settling lets the move land first, and the key makes a release followed by a re-seat one clear rather than two. It is scheduled rather than deferred to a frame, so a session driven by [method MultiplayerAPI.poll] alone still closes the window.

method.name: scene_seat_clear_key
method.description: The settle key [method scene_seat_clear_deferred] coalesces under, which is per [param peer] and per [param scene] rather than global: two peers leaving one scene in a pump are two clears, and one peer's repeated release edges against one scene are one.

method.name: scene_seat_release_key
method.description: The settle key a departing player's seat release coalesces under, which is per [param peer] and per [param scene]. A node that leaves and re-enters within one pump settles [method scene_release_departed] once, and the answer it gives is read from the tree as it stands at the settle rather than as it stood at either edge. It is distinct from [method scene_seat_clear_key] because the two windows answer different questions about the same peer: one tells a release from a move, the other tells a free from a reparent, and a shared key would let either swallow the other.

method.name: scene_seat_sync
method.description: Seats [param peer] in whichever live scene it is aware of, answering that scene or an invalid [RID] when it is aware of none. A client computes no admission of its own, so its seat is something it is told, and awareness of the scene entity itself is the only form the telling can take: a peer admitted to a scene sees that scene's container, and a peer released from it stops seeing it. The scene entity's own presence in the scene's boundary roster is therefore read as the seat. Only the scene each stem currently answers with is considered, so the shadowed sibling of a re-entered stem is passed over, and the first match wins. A [param peer] the roster never opened is seated nowhere, because a seat belongs to a participant row. The seat is written through [method participant_seat_move], so the peer's row hears the change. A peer aware of nothing keeps the seat it holds rather than losing it, because awareness arriving late is the ordinary case and an empty read is not a release. [method scene_released_seat] is what clears a seat on purpose.

method.name: scene_send_result
method.description: Sends the terminal answer to [param peer]'s [param request_id] on the scene-result channel, reliably and unbatched. This writes the frame [method NetwSceneCore.receive_result_frame] reads, and the two are the whole of the result wire. They live beside each other so the shape they agree on has one owner: a sender that spelled the row itself would be a second copy of that agreement, free to drift a field at a time with nothing failing until a peer decodes a request id as a code.

method.name: scene_set_request_handler
method.description: Installs [param handler] as the single door deciding player scene requests. It receives [code](participant, destination, args)[/code] and answers an [enum @GlobalScope.Error]: [constant @GlobalScope.OK] admits the request, anything else refuses it and becomes the promise's settle code. One owner rather than a veto signal, because several listeners refusing one request has no defined resolution. An unset [Callable] uninstalls, restoring the consent line the session decides by when no game policy is installed, so uninstalling is the same act as never installing.

method.name: scene_spawn
method.description: Constructs and replicates a scene from [param data], parents it under the spawn anchor, and answers the mounted container or [code]null[/code] when the spawn produced nothing. [param data] is a resource path unless the session declared a [member NetwSceneConfig.level_spawn_function], which receives it verbatim on every peer. The spawn goes through [method spawn_registered] on [method scene_constructor_id], so the container is reconstructed by the registry rather than by a manager node, and every peer runs the same constructor. [param isolation] declares whether this one scene hosts its own world, as a [enum NetwSceneCore.Isolation]. It rides the recipe, so two scenes in one session may differ, and [code]-1[/code] takes the session's declared default. [method NetwSceneCore.spawn_note] warns first when the new scene would share one physics space with a live one. The parent is [method NetwSceneCore.spawn_anchor], falling back to [method session_root]. A spawn with neither leaves the container orphaned and still answers it, because the entity is already live and dropping the node would strand it.

method.name: scene_spawn_declared
method.description: Brings up the declared scene named [param stem] from its declared path, answering the mounted container, the one already live under that stem, or [code]null[/code] when the stem was never declared. It is [method scene_spawn] with the path read off the declaration instead of supplied, so a caller that knows a stem never has to know where it lives. A stem already live is answered as it stands rather than spawned twice, which is what makes a startup spawn safe to run after a join has already brought the scene online.

method.name: scene_spawn_initial
method.description: Brings up every stem the declaration marked initial that is not already live. It is the server's startup pass, and it announces nothing: the caller that publishes a startup-complete signal emits it after this returns. A stem a join already brought online is skipped, which is what the stem answers for, and a stem with no declared path is skipped silently.

method.name: scene_spawn_node
method.description: Builds the orphan container one scene mounts under, from [param data] and the [enum NetwSceneCore.Isolation] the spawn declared. This is the session's scene constructor: it is registered through [method spawn_register_constructor] and therefore runs on every peer, so what it builds must depend on its two arguments alone. [param data] is a resource path unless a declaration supplied [method NetwSceneCore.declared_level_spawn_function], which then receives [param data] verbatim. [param isolation] rides the recipe rather than session state, so two live scenes in one session may isolate differently. The container is [method scene_build_container]'s, the content is mounted with [method scene_install_level], and the container's own entity record is stamped with [member NetwEntity.declares_scene] and [member NetwEntity.scene_label] before the spawn arms, so the record plane resolves a mounted scene with no node walk behind it. Every peer runs this, so the value a SPAWN packet carries is the value the receiver already wrote. The two callables [method NetwSceneCore.set_container_lifecycle] holds are connected to the container's [signal Node.tree_entered] and [signal Node.tree_exited] here, because this is the only point that sees a container while it is still an orphan. Answers [code]null[/code] when the declared builder answers nothing, when [param data] names no scene, and when [param data] is neither.

method.name: scene_stem
method.description: The non-unique stem [param scene] answers to: the label a script declared through [member NetwEntity.scene_label], and otherwise the content root's name. Empty for a scene no record stands for. One answer rather than two, because the content root's name is the key the live book files a scene under, so a caller that read the two separately would be comparing one fact spelled twice.

method.name: scene_unobserve
method.description: Reverses [method scene_observe] for one [param callback]. Removing something never registered is inert rather than an error.

method.name: scenes_named
method.description: Every live scene whose stem is [param stem], in the order they entered. Empty when the stem names none.

method.name: schema_add_column
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.add_column] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: schema_create
method.description: The handle for the schema named [param name], minting one when this session holds none. Declaring a name that already exists answers the handle it already has and restarts that schema's re-declaration cursor, so a script reload replays its own columns rather than minting a second schema.

method.name: schema_find
method.description: The handle this session holds for [param name], or an invalid [RID] when it holds none. The lookup alone. Compiling a declaration this session has not adopted stays above the core, because a registry of declarations is GDScript and a core that read one would be reaching back across the seam it defines.

method.name: schema_get_column_count
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.column_count] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: schema_get_column_key
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.column_key] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: schema_get_column_stride
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.column_stride] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: schema_get_column_type
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.column_type] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: schema_get_hash
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.hash_of] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: schema_seal
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.seal] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: schema_set_column_quantizer
method.description: Forwards to [method SchemaCore.set_column_quantizer] on the schema core this session owns.

method.name: send_datagram
method.description: Frames one datagram and hands it to the transport. Answers the sequence it went out under, or [code]-1[/code] for a reliable datagram and for a refusal. A refusal is a datagram that was never sent, so the two share an answer here only because neither has a sequence to report.

method.name: send_to
method.description: Sends one payload to [param peer], choosing for itself how it travels. The one send verb the session publishes, because the three ways a payload can leave are one decision and a caller that picked among them would have to know the clock and the channel declaration to pick correctly. [codeblock] peer is us dispatched locally, never framed clock configured, channel appended to the peer's run, flushed by aggregates [method carrier_flush] otherwise framed and sent now [/codeblock] Aggregation waits on [method carrier_flush], which the tick pump calls, so a session with no configured clock never aggregates: a buffered frame would sit in the run forever. When an append displaces a run, the sequence that run went out under is reported back so a pass staged this tick can be committed against it. A negative [param route] is refused with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER], because it addresses no entity and no peer-scoped stream either.

method.name: seq_is_fresher
method.description: Whether [param a] is fresher than [param b] on the u16 ring, judged across the half window so a wrap reads as an advance and a reorder does not.

method.name: service_all
method.description: Every service whose script is [param base] or derives from it, in registration order.

method.name: service_clear
method.description: Drops every registered service. Silent, because a session that is ending announces its own end and a per-service notice would repeat what every listener has already been told.

method.name: service_of
method.description: The service registered under [param type], or [code]null[/code]. A service the game freed reads as absent, because the book holds an id rather than a reference: keeping one would outlive the scene that made it.

method.name: service_register
method.description: Registers [param service] under [param type], defaulting to its own script, and emits [signal service_registered]. Re-registering the identical instance is inert, because a service that auto-registers on entering the tree may also be registered explicitly.

method.name: service_unregister
method.description: The twin of [method service_register], honoured only while [param type] still names [param service].

method.name: session_accepted_join
method.description: The join this session accepted for [param peer], or [code]null[/code] while it has not been admitted. It is the same book [method session_admit] writes, so a reader here and the admission never disagree about who joined.

method.name: session_accepted_joins
method.description: Every accepted [ResolvedJoin] this session knows, in the order the peers were admitted. A client's copy holds what the accept and roster frames brought it, so it is this peer's knowledge rather than the server's truth.

method.name: session_admit
method.description: Admits [param join], remembering it in the accepted-join book, ensuring the peer's participant row, marking that row admitted, and announcing [signal participant_joined]. Idempotent per peer: a join the book already holds unchanged is dropped, so the accept frame and the roster backfill can both carry it and the peer is announced once. On server authority the join handler installed by [method set_session_join_handler] runs between the admission and the announcement. That order is the contract: the handler may seat the participant in a scene, and a consumer of [signal participant_joined] is entitled to read the seat the join produced.

method.name: session_clear_roster
method.description: Forgets every accepted join and every refusal. The participant rows are not touched: a row outlives the join that enriched it, so tearing the roster down does not retract peers that are still connected.

method.name: session_forget_peer
method.description: Drops [param peer]'s accepted join and its refusal reason, so a peer that reconnects is admitted afresh rather than inheriting the verdict of its last visit.

method.name: session_free_name
method.description: The first variant of [param name] that no entry of [param taken] holds. Answered only for a name [method session_name_verdict] returned [constant NAME_RENAME] for; calling it on a name that was refused would paper over the refusal.

method.name: session_kick
method.description: Removes [param peer_id] from the session on server authority, announcing [signal kicked] to that peer first when [param reason] is non-empty. A session without server authority refuses the call and removes nobody. The notice is sent before the transport peer closes, because a closed peer carries nothing: the kicked client learns why only if the frame precedes its disconnection.

method.name: session_name_verdict
method.description: What to do about a peer arriving as [param name] while [param taken] already holds those names: [constant NAME_ADMIT], [constant NAME_RENAME], or [constant NAME_REFUSE]. The two flags are what separate the three answers. A debug join renames around a collision, because a developer running several clients wants all of them in. An authenticated join refuses, because the name came from a service and silently altering it would make the roster disagree with the account. Everything else is admitted, collision or not, and the caller warns. The caller supplies [param taken] rather than this session reading it, because what counts as a live name is the game's question and the answer differs by whether an entity carries an authored id.

method.name: session_notify_shutdown
method.description: Warns every live peer that this server is going away, carrying [param reason], and announces [signal server_disconnecting] locally as well. A session without server authority refuses the call and warns nobody. The notice rides a session control channel rather than a node [code]@rpc[/code], so a session with no scene tree still warns its clients. It only announces: nothing here closes a peer, so the server remains responsible for its own teardown afterwards.

method.name: session_pause
method.description: Suspends the game on every live peer, each receiving [signal tree_paused] carrying [param reason], and on this session too. A session without server authority refuses the call and pauses nobody. The local announcement is made through the same channel decode a remote peer takes, so the host cannot end up in a pause state its clients disagree with.

method.name: session_publish_control
method.description: Announces the session control frame [param channel] carries, and answers whether it was consumed here. The channel decides which announcement it is, the authority rule decides whether this session honours it at all, and the payload decodes the same way for every one of them; those three are one decision, so a caller routes a frame here rather than keeping a copy of the mapping. Consumed and refused are the same answer, [code]true[/code]: the channel was this band's, so a caller must not fall through and route it elsewhere. A channel outside the band answers [code]false[/code].

method.name: session_receive_join
method.description: Takes one inbound join request from [param sender] on server authority: it is refused past the flood window, decoded into a [JoinPayload] stamped with the sender's peer id, resolved through the [Callable] installed by [method set_session_join_resolver], then admitted through [method session_admit], announced to every live peer, and answered to a remote sender with the accepted-join roster it missed. The sender is the frame's, never the payload's, so a client cannot claim a peer id it does not hold. A host submitting its own join calls this directly with sender 1, which is why the local and remote paths cannot diverge.

method.name: session_refusal
method.description: Why [param peer] was refused, or an empty string when it was not. Held past the refusal itself so the disconnect can carry a reason the peer can be told.

method.name: session_refuse
method.description: Records [param reason] as why [param peer] is not admitted. It only records: refusing does not close the peer, so the caller that decided still owns the disconnect.

method.name: session_remember_join
method.description: Stores [param join] in the accepted book, answering whether it was new or was enriched from an argless row into an arg-carrying one. It is the storage half of [method session_admit] with none of the announcement, for a caller that is rebuilding a roster rather than admitting a peer.

method.name: session_request_kick
method.description: Asks server authority to remove [param peer_id], carrying [param reason] with the request. The server announces it as [signal kick_requested] and decides; nothing here removes anyone, which is what separates this from [method session_kick]. The request rides a session control channel rather than a node [code]@rpc[/code], so a session with no scene tree still asks. A session that already holds authority publishes the request to itself, so the server's own handler is the single place the decision is taken.

method.name: session_request_leave
method.description: Asks server authority for permission to leave, carrying [param reason]. The server announces it as [signal disconnect_requested] and decides; nothing here closes a peer or leaves a session. A session that already holds authority publishes the request to itself, so the server's own handler is the single place the decision is taken.

method.name: session_root
method.description: The node this session roots relative addressing at, or [code]null[/code] while none is installed or the one that was has been freed. It is read through the [Callable] installed by [method set_session_root] rather than resolved here, because resolving it means walking a [SceneTree] from a path, and this session takes its ambient state as arguments so it stays drivable with no tree at all. It is the fallback [method NetwSceneCore.spawn_anchor] takes when a declaration named no anchor, and the parent a session-owned view is mounted under, so both survive a native scene change alongside the session content.

method.name: session_unpause
method.description: Resumes the game on every live peer, each receiving [signal tree_unpaused], and on this session too. A session without server authority refuses the call and resumes nobody. The twin of [method session_pause], and unconditional: it carries no reason and does not check that a pause preceded it, because a peer that missed the pause must still end up resumed.

method.name: set_desired_role_reader
method.description: Installs [param reader] as the [Callable] [method authored_desired_role] answers from. It takes no arguments and answers a [enum Role]. A [Callable] rather than a pushed value, because the authored role is a configuration a game re-authors between the edges that resolve a role, and that is exactly the difference between this and the machine's own desired role, set through [method session_set_desired_role]. Pushing it here would collapse the two into one fact and lose the distinction the next edge depends on.

method.name: set_display_authors_streams
method.description: Installs the [Callable] answering [method display_authors_streams] for a runtime.

method.name: set_display_chase_clamp
method.description: Installs [param clamp] as the [Callable] answering the largest render offset a chase absorption may hold for a runtime, which is that entity's own teleport tier: an offset past it would show a pose a teleport was entitled to snap through. Read only by [method display_absorb_recovery]. With none installed the offset is unclamped, which is the right answer for an entity that declares no teleport threshold.

method.name: set_display_chase_hook
method.description: Installs the [Callable] that subscribes a chasing runtime to its entity's reconciliation writes, called as [code](runtime, bind)[/code] and expected to drop the subscription when [code]bind[/code] is false. A chase absorbs corrections; every other role does not, so the subscription follows the role rather than the entity.

method.name: set_display_lane
method.description: Installs [param lane] as the display door every channel this session builds is given, called as [code](entity, target_prop, value)[/code] and answering an [enum @GlobalScope.Error]. See [member NetwDisplayChannel.door] for what its verdict decides.

method.name: set_display_role_facts
method.description: Installs the [Callable] answering a [NetwDisplayRoleFacts] for a runtime, called as [code](runtime, authors_streams)[/code]. It answers the facts only the prediction handle and entity control know. The stream half is decided here and passed in, and [member NetwDisplayRoleFacts.owner_is_authority] is filled here afterwards, so each field has exactly one author.

method.name: set_display_role_resolver
method.description: Installs [param resolver] as the [Callable] that decides a runtime's [member NetwDisplayRuntime.pump_mode] from its control, authority and authored streams. Called by [method display_pump_runtime] only for a runtime reading [constant NetwDisplayDecl.PUMP_UNRESOLVED], so resolution is event-driven rather than a per-frame scan, and the kernels never read authority at all.

method.name: set_display_spec_reader
method.description: Installs the [Callable] that answers what a node's subtree declares for display, as an [Array] of [NetwDisplaySpecRow], called as [code](owner)[/code]. This is the ONE door to the authoring registry. A session with no reader installed builds no channels at all, rather than building an empty display it would have to repair later.

method.name: set_display_sync_intervals
method.description: Installs the [Callable] that reads an entity's synchronizers and derived state binding to set the runtime's expected snapshot interval, called as [code](runtime)[/code]. Read when a runtime enters [constant NetwDisplayDecl.PUMP_REMOTE], because the interval only decides how deep the jitter buffer for a played-back stream has to be.

method.name: set_identity_reader
method.description: Installs [param reader] as what [method participant_identity] asks. It receives [code](peer)[/code] and answers a [NetwIdentity] or [code]null[/code]. A [Callable] rather than a read performed here, because auth buckets are keyed by a GDScript [Script] type and this session cannot name one. With none installed every identity is [code]null[/code], which is also the answer a session with no auth provider gives.

method.name: set_inner
method.description: Replaces the transport [method get_inner] answers with [param inner], relaying its peer-authenticating and peer-authentication-failed signals from the new transport and dropping the relay from whichever it replaces. Setting the transport it already holds does nothing.

method.name: set_interest_awareness_send
method.description: Installs [param send] as the [Callable] a flush hands one peer's outgoing awareness batch to. It receives the peer id and the encoded wire [Array], and is expected to carry that array to the peer as a reliable, route-addressed frame on the awareness channel [method interest_receive_awareness] decodes on the other end. With none installed, a flush computes the batch but delivers it nowhere.

method.name: set_interest_compat_refresh
method.description: Installs [param refresh] as the [Callable] called back whenever a peer connecting or disconnecting actually changes the live-peer set behind [method interest_known_peers]. It takes no arguments and is expected to rebuild every compat-adapter intent row that a peer joining or leaving invalidates. With none installed, a live-peer change updates the committed set but rebuilds no compat intent.

method.name: set_interest_flush
method.description: Installs [param flush] as the [Callable] [method interest_request_flush] schedules, which is the one door between an interest write and the recompute that publishes it. Install it once, beside the layer factory, before any admission can be made. [method interest_request_flush] refuses and counts a verdict while none is installed rather than dropping the request, because the cost of a missing flush is a matrix that stays stale and still reads as valid.

method.name: set_interest_visibility_sweep
method.description: Installs [param sweep] as the [Callable] a committed interest change schedules to reconcile spawn visibility against the new admissions. It takes no arguments and is expected to settle a visibility sweep rather than run one inline, so several admissions collapsed into one flush still produce one sweep. With none installed, the committed matrix changes but no peer's spawned recipient set follows it.

method.name: set_layer_factory
method.description: Installs [param factory] as the builder [method layer_open] calls to produce a view for a name with no layer open yet. It receives the name and answers the view, so the session owns the book of layers while whatever installed the factory owns what a layer presents.

method.name: set_layer_lookup
method.description: Installs [param lookup] as the [Callable] [method scene_layer_view] reads a layer through. It receives the layer id and answers the view, or [code]null[/code] when no layer of that name is open. It is the twin of [method set_layer_factory] and deliberately not the same [Callable]. The factory MINTS, so installing it here would make every read of an admission boundary open one, and a scene nobody was ever admitted to would then report an empty boundary rather than no boundary at all. With none installed [method scene_layer_view] reports and answers [code]null[/code], because a session whose layers cannot be read is a defect in whatever built it rather than something a peer did.

method.name: set_peer_ids
method.description: Replaces the peer id list this session answers its [MultiplayerAPI] override of [code]get_peers[/code] from.

method.name: set_replication_plane
method.description: Where the replication plane lives while it is still script-owned. The session is told once rather than reached through the shell, so a native verb that needs it asks the session and not its GDScript twin.

method.name: set_request_deadline_arm
method.description: Installs [param arm] as the [Callable] [method scene_request_open] delegates a request's wait to. It receives the request id and the deadline in seconds, and owes a call to [method scene_request_expire] with that id once the wait elapses. A [Callable] rather than a timer held here, because waiting means a [SceneTree] and this session never touches one. With none installed, [method scene_request_open] still sends, and the request it opened waits for authority with no deadline behind it.

method.name: set_scene_carry_move
method.description: Installs [param carry] as the [Callable] [method scene_move_entity] hands a reachable move to. It receives [code](mover, destination_node, opts, promise)[/code] and owns everything from the physics guard to settling [code]promise[/code]. A [Callable] rather than work done here, because the guarded reparent is a window measured in physics frames, and this session advances on its own ticks and never touches a [SceneTree]. The carry subscribes to those frames and answers later, which is why it is handed the promise rather than returning a value. With none installed, [method scene_move_entity] rejects every move [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE], which is the same answer an unreachable destination gets: no move happened, and the caller is told so.

method.name: set_scene_mark_reader
method.description: Installs [param reader] as the [Callable] [method scene_mark_of] reads a scene root's declaration through. It receives a [Script] and answers a [NetwSceneMark]. A [Callable] rather than a table held here, because a mark is authored against a [Script] by [method Netw.mark_multiplayer_scene] and [method Netw.configure_multiplayer_scene], both of which run from script-tier constructors before any session exists. Install one reader and every door reads through it, rather than each door reaching into the authoring tier for the field it happens to need. With none installed, [method scene_mark_of] answers a blank mark, which admits nothing and captures nothing.

method.name: set_scene_participant_edge
method.description: Installs [param edge] as the [Callable] [method scene_admit_peer] and [method scene_release_peer] report a changed boundary to. It receives [code](scene, peer, present)[/code]. One installed reporter rather than a report at each call site, because admission is written from several places, a scene change, a departure and a spawn among them, and a boundary written without its edge reported leaves a participant presenting a scene it no longer belongs to with nothing to observe. It fires only when the boundary actually changed, so a repeated admission reports nothing, and it fires after the flush is requested, so what it announces is what the committed matrix is already scheduled to publish. With none installed the boundary is still written and still flushed. Only the announcement is lost.

method.name: set_scene_path_reader
method.description: Installs [param reader] as the [Callable] [method scene_request_targets] asks for the resource path declared under a label. [param reader] receives the label and answers the path, or an empty [String] when the label declares none.

method.name: set_scene_refresh
method.description: Installs [param refresh] as the [Callable] [method scene_despawn] schedules on the settle queue after a lingering despawn, so the peer's current scene is re-read once the retirement has landed.

method.name: set_session_join_handler
method.description: Installs the [Callable] [method session_admit] runs for each peer it admits on server authority, called with that peer's id. It resolves and invokes the game's own join handler, which is script that may await, so it is installed rather than implemented here. It is called and not waited on. A handler that suspends resumes on its own continuation, and the admission announcement does not wait for it.

method.name: set_session_join_resolver
method.description: Installs the [Callable] [method session_receive_join] resolves an inbound request with, called as [code]resolver(payload, sender)[/code] and answering the [ResolvedJoin] to admit or [code]null[/code] to reject. Decoding the wire arguments against the game's join handler, resolving an authenticated identity and running the admission gate are all script, so the verdict is installed rather than decided here. A session with no resolver installed admits nobody, because an open gate and an unconfigured one are indistinguishable from here and only one of them is safe.

method.name: set_session_root
method.description: Installs [param reader] as the [Callable] [method session_root] answers from. It takes no arguments and answers the node, which is what lets the answer follow a re-mount without anything here being told about it. A [Callable] rather than a stored node, because the root is derived from the transport's own relative-addressing path and re-resolves when that path changes. A node pushed once would go stale silently, and a stale root parents a session's own views under a branch that is no longer in the tree.

method.name: set_spawn_pipeline
method.description: Where the spawn pipeline lives while it is still script-owned, so a session verb reaches it without the shell naming it. Installed the moment the pipeline exists rather than at the end of session construction, because everything built after it can already register a constructor, and every spawn verb below refuses while the session has nobody to reach.

method.name: set_spawn_state_gather
method.description: Registers how this session answers "which marked properties ride a spawn". [param gather] takes the template node and answers an [Array] of [code]{node, prop}[/code] rows in the order the receiver applies them. The declaration registry is script-owned, so the session is told once rather than reaching into it per instantiation. A session told nothing carries nothing.

method.name: set_sync_pipeline
method.description: Where the sync pipeline lives while it is still script-owned, installed exactly as [method set_spawn_pipeline] is and for the same reason.

method.name: set_wrapper_factory
method.description: Registers how to build an entity wrapper. [param factory] takes the root node and answers the wrapper, already attached to it. Process-wide and outliving every session, because an entity is constructed, configured and read before any session exists, exactly as [NetwEntityIds] is. The extension drops the factory at shutdown.

method.name: settle_advance
method.description: Spends one pump against every window [method settle_schedule_after] is holding. Separate from the drain, because a clocked session drains on its polls as well as its ticks and a window is counted in the cadence the session sends at. Calling it twice a pump spends the window twice.

method.name: settle_cancel
method.description: Withdraws [param key] from the queue, for a caller that did the work on the spot and has nothing left to settle. An unqueued key is not an error.

method.name: settle_clear
method.description: Drops every queued row without running any of them.

method.name: settle_drain
method.description: Flushes staged event emissions, then runs every due row to a fixed point, a pass at a time, each pass taking the whole queue so a row scheduled during a pass runs in the next pass rather than inside the one that scheduled it. Answers the keys still pending when [method settle_max_passes] was hit, empty when the drain reached a fixed point; an unkeyed row answers [code]"<unkeyed>"[/code], because the report exists to name a cycle and an empty string names nothing. A row whose [method settle_schedule_after] window is still open is waiting rather than cycling, so it is neither run nor reported nor dropped.

method.name: settle_has_key
method.description: Whether [param key] is queued. A named key coalesces, so the answer is the whole of how many of it are pending.

method.name: settle_max_passes
method.description: The pass bound [method settle_drain] gives up at. A cascade that has not settled in this many passes is a cycle rather than a deep chain, and a defect that hangs is worse than one that reports.

method.name: settle_pending
method.description: How many rows are queued, unkeyed rows counted individually and each named key counted once.

method.name: settle_schedule
method.description: Schedules [param fn] to run at the next [method settle_drain]. A named [param key] coalesces: scheduling a key already queued moves it to the back, which is what "run after the cascade that scheduled me" means. An empty key never coalesces, so unkeyed rows run in the order they were scheduled.

method.name: settle_schedule_after
method.description: Holds [param fn] for [param pumps] pumps before a settle will run it. A window counted in the session's own pumps needs no [SceneTree] and no wall clock, so a teardown that has to stay reachable for a while is expressible where a scene tree is not. [param key] coalesces exactly as it does for [method settle_schedule], so re-declaring a window replaces it rather than queuing a second one. A window still open is not a settle that failed to reach a fixed point, so it is never reported as one.

method.name: sink_verdict
method.description: Counts one remote-input [param verdict] on [param route], says whatever it is worth saying, and answers the verdict. The three things a verdict is worth are one partition rather than three call sites. A route this peer has not seen, one that is dead and one whose node is gone are ordinary traffic and stay silent. [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED], [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA] and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_BUSY] name a sender that sent what it may not, and warn once per verdict and route together, so one peer retrying cannot flood a log. Anything outside the partition is this session's own defect and is reported as an error, because a sink that answered something which is not a verdict has a bug rather than a new row. [constant @GlobalScope.OK] is not a verdict. It counts nothing and reports nothing, which is why a gate that admitted a frame is visible through [method gate_verdict] and not here.

method.name: spawn_admit_frame_default
method.description: The stock verdict on one inbound spawn, despawn or reparent frame, and the body an override of the spawn admission seam narrows rather than replaces. Materialization is server-authored, so [param sender] is judged before anything else: a peer other than the server is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] whatever channel it named. A channel outside the three this gate admits, or an empty [param payload], is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA]. [param route] is unresolved by construction, because the frame that creates a route arrives before that route exists. It travels so an override can read it.

method.name: spawn_adopt
method.description: Takes one node that is already in the scene into replication, answering its entity handle. The entity is armed where it stands rather than reconstructed, so peers that already hold the node keep it. An invalid [RID] means the pipeline declined it.

method.name: spawn_function
method.description: Runs [param function] and replicates what it built, answering the entity handle. The function must answer an orphan node, which the caller then places. An invalid [RID] means it answered nothing.

method.name: spawn_register_constructor
method.description: Registers [param function] under [param id], so [method spawn_registered] can reconstruct it on a peer that has no host node to read it from. [param arg_types] and [param quantizers] declare positionally how [param function]'s arguments cross the wire. Declaring them keys the argument schema to [param id], which is how the wire already addresses the recipe, so a [param function] whose object carries no [Script] still encodes and decodes. Declaring neither reads the schema off the host script instead, which then has to answer identically on every peer. A schema is the recipe's own law rather than a negotiated one: every peer registers [param id] locally and decodes with what it registered, so two peers declaring different schemas for one id read different values out of the same bytes.

method.name: spawn_registered
method.description: Runs the constructor registered under [param id] on every peer and answers the local entity handle. The mirror of [method spawn_function] for a session with no host node: the recipe is an id both sides already hold rather than a reference only the sender has.

method.name: spawn_replicate
method.description: Arms [param node] for replicated construction and answers its entity handle. An invalid [RID] means the pipeline declined the node, which is the same answer a session with no pipeline installed gives.

method.name: spawn_state_of
method.description: The authored spawn state [param entity]'s subtree contributes, in the order a receiver applies it. Empty for an entity whose owner is gone, because the state is read off the live subtree rather than remembered.

method.name: stage_verdict
method.description: Records that [param stage] ran on [param route] and answered [param verdict], and answers the verdict back, so a caller reads the stage and its answer as one expression. [param stage] is a gate ([constant GATE_SYNC], [constant GATE_SPAWN], [constant GATE_TABLE], [constant GATE_PREDICT]) or a pipeline stage ([constant SPAWN_DECLARE], [constant SPAWN_RECONCILE] and the rest of that range). A watched session gets one row of that kind for every run, including the ones that answered [constant @GlobalScope.OK], because "this stage ran and admitted it" is the fact an observer most often wants and the one a verdict count cannot carry. Everything else the verdict is worth is [method sink_verdict]'s, so a stage cannot count its answer one way and report it another.

method.name: sync_send_property
method.description: Sends one configured property of one component now, outside the tick pump. [codeblock] Error ┠╴OK the property was handed to the sync lane ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST [param comp] resolves to no live node ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA the node declares no such property [/codeblock]

method.name: sync_send_signal
method.description: Sends one configured signal of one component, with [param args] as its arguments. Refuses exactly as [method sync_send_property] does, on an unresolvable component and on a signal the node does not declare.

method.name: table_admit_frame_default
method.description: The stock verdict on one inbound table frame, and the body an override of the table admission seam narrows rather than replaces. It takes no route because a table frame is route-0 addressed and the routes it carries are knowable only mid-decode, so everything it judges is in the header: who sent it, which table it names, and whether that table's sealed schema agrees. A frame from a peer other than the server is counted on [member table_core] as well as refused, because the count is what separates a rejected sender from a table nobody is publishing.

method.name: table_commit
method.description: Fixes [param table]'s written routes and columns as the applied state readers compare against. Stamped with the session's own tick, because a commit is what fixes the frame a reader dates itself against and two clocks would date it twice.

method.name: table_create
method.description: A table over [param schema], keyed by the schema's name. Binding a schema whose name already carries a table answers that table, so a script reload finds its own handle rather than minting a second one. An unsealed schema has no address order yet and is refused.

method.name: table_find
method.description: The handle [method table_create] minted for [param name]'s sealed schema, or an invalid [RID] when it has minted none.

method.name: table_get_row
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.row_of] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_get_rows
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.rows_of] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_get_schema
method.description: The schema [method table_create] sealed [param table] from, or an invalid [RID] when [param table] is not one this session created.

method.name: table_get_tick
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.tick_of] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_get_wire_hash
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.schema_hash] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_publish
method.description: Announces one table as [signal table_received], stamped with the tick its commit fixed. For the send side, where a commit made this tick is announced beside the ones an intake produced.

method.name: table_publish_intake
method.description: Announces every table this tick's intake touched, then opens the next intake window. The two are one act: announcing without reopening announces the same tables again next tick, and reopening without announcing loses the wave. The set is [member table_core]'s own, so a table the decoder never wrote to is never named.

method.name: table_read_births
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.read_births] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_read_column
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.read_column] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_read_deaths
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.read_deaths] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_read_routes
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.read_routes] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_set_param
method.description: Sets one [enum TableParam] on [param table] to [param value]. [param param] outside [enum TableParam] changes nothing.

method.name: table_write_column
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.write_column] on [member table_core].

method.name: table_write_routes
method.description: Forwards to [method TableCore.write_routes] on [member table_core].

method.name: verdict_total
method.description: How many times [param verdict] has been counted by [method count_verdict] since the last [method clear_verdicts].

method.name: warn_verdict
method.description: Counts [param verdict] on [param route] and answers whether this occurrence is the one that may speak. Every occurrence counts, so [method verdict_total] still reads the true rate, and only the first of a [param verdict] and [param route] pair claims the warning, so a peer retrying a refused act cannot flood a log however often it does. Counting and claiming are one act because a caller that did either alone would either undercount a refusal or warn on every repeat. The message itself stays with the caller, which is what keeps a release build from formatting one it will not print.

method.name: wrapper_adopt
method.description: Introduces [param wrapper] to this session under [param entity], so the index answers for it. Idempotent, and it never mints. [b]This index is the one place an entity wrapper is held.[/b] A wrapper is reference counted and nothing else keeps it alive, so the index holds a reference rather than an id: an id-only index frees the wrapper the moment the caller that made it lets go, and every later resolve answers a dead object.

method.name: wrapper_at
method.description: The wrapper at or above [param node], read from [method wrapper_meta] metadata, or [code]null[/code] when the walk finds none. An unmarked node in between is not an entity, so the walk passes through it rather than stopping.

method.name: wrapper_bind
method.description: Names [param node] after the identity and stamps it onto the node's wrapper, minting one through [method set_wrapper_factory] when the node carries none. An [param entity_id] the codec cannot name binds NOTHING, because a name that spells no identity would leave the node and the record disagreeing about who the entity is.

method.name: wrapper_clear
method.description: Drops both sides of the index. Session teardown.

method.name: wrapper_ensure
method.description: The wrapper on [param root] itself, minted through [method set_wrapper_factory] when it carries none. A node is given one wrapper and keeps it, so two callers asking answer the same object.

method.name: wrapper_for_id
method.description: Live or retired, which is the door an engine resolves a delta row through: a removed entity's last act is a hide to every peer that held it, and the transition naming it arrives in the NEXT delta.

method.name: wrapper_for_route
method.description: The route-keyed twin of [method wrapper_of].

method.name: wrapper_live
method.description: Every wrapper this peer holds a live route for, ordered by route so two calls in one frame agree.

method.name: wrapper_meta
method.description: The metadata an entity root carries its wrapper in. One spelling, shared by the wrapper that writes it and every walk that reads it.

method.name: wrapper_of
method.description: The live wrapper carrying [param entity], or [code]null[/code]. A wrapper a death retired is not live and answers [code]null[/code] here; [method wrapper_for_id] still finds it.

method.name: wrapper_owner
method.description: The root node [param entity] names, or [code]null[/code] once the tree has freed it. Held by id rather than by reference, because the tree owns it.

method.name: wrapper_resolve
method.description: The wrapper for [param node], provisioned on the topmost orphan above it when nothing in the chain carries one. A record provisioned on the leaf would name a node that is about to become somebody else's child. Answers [code]null[/code] once the tree holds [param node] or any of its ancestors, because that is past the moment a record could be provisioned. Use [method wrapper_ensure] to force one onto an exact node.

method.name: wrapper_sweep_retired
method.description: Drops every wrapper a death retired, one full cycle after the retirement, which is the moment the index's last grip on it goes.

members.member: Which handler answers for each wire channel, on both the entity lane and the peer-scoped one. It is the session's rather than any one interface's, because a registration has to outlive the interface that made it: every core writes its own rows here at construction and the replication interface dissolves before they do.

The session's clock, minted with the session and running for its whole life. [member NetwMultiplayer.clock] is this object, so a caller holding one never has to re-fetch it after a [MultiplayerClock] registers or leaves.

The scene this peer presents, or an invalid [RID]. A dedicated server presents nothing and always answers invalid. Read-only here: it is recomputed from what the session seats this peer in rather than written by whatever changed, so a scene arriving, leaving or re-seating this peer all settle through one answer.

Whether this peer holds server authority, as either a dedicated or a listen server. Distinct from [member is_server], which answers peer IDENTITY: a peer can carry unique id 1 before the session machine has resolved any role at all.

The entity this peer is represented by, or [code]null[/code] when none represents it. The handle is kept beside the wrapper rather than looked up by route, because a retirement has to ask whether the DYING entity is the one representing this peer, and asking that by route answers yes for every entity that has one. A scene change spawns the replacement before retiring the original, so a route-keyed test drops a local player that had already moved on.

The authoritative timeline store, one slot per entity a state set declares, and the substrate a server rewind reads. It is the session's rather than the lag-compensation interface's for the same reason [member channel_book] is: an entity registers a timeline when its state set registers, which outlives any one interface, and two stores would be two histories that agree only by accident.

How far an admitted scene request reaches, using the ordinals [code]NetwMultiplayer.SceneReach[/code] publishes: zero moves only the requesting participant, one moves the whole session. Server policy rather than something a requester may ask for, and it defaults to the participant because a request names one participant and moving the rest of the session is a larger claim than the requester made. A reach outside the enum names nothing and is refused rather than stored for a later request to be measured against, so a write that does not take leaves the reach that was already in force.

What the display plane holds for each entity, addressed by the entity's [RID] or by its route. On the session plane rather than on the display core, so a read that only needs a row does not need the core.

signal.name: after_tick
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] at the end of each tick, after game logic. The clock announces on the session rather than on itself, so a consumer holding the session never has to hold the clock and there is one place a tick can be subscribed to.

signal.name: after_tick_loop
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] once after [method NetwClockHandle.physics_step]'s tick loop finishes, whether or not it ran a tick. Not announced by [method NetwClockHandle.force_step], which is a step rather than a frame.

signal.name: before_tick
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] at the start of each tick, before game logic.

signal.name: before_tick_loop
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] once before [method NetwClockHandle.physics_step]'s tick loop runs, whether or not it will run a tick. Not announced by [method NetwClockHandle.force_step], which is a step rather than a frame.

signal.name: clock_synchronized
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] once, when its first calibration lands. A later [method NetwClockHandle.handle_pong] recalibrates without re-announcing.

signal.name: disconnect_requested
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when a client asks to leave. Heard only by a session holding peer id 1, and [param peer_id] is the frame's sender rather than anything the payload claims.

signal.name: display_offset_insufficient
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] when [member NetwClockHandle.recommended_display_offset] rises above [member NetwClockHandle.display_offset]. Latched, so worsening conditions do not repeat it, and it can fire again once conditions recover and degrade a second time.

signal.name: entity_dead
signal.description: Emitted by [method liveness_retire]. The wrapper has already left the live index for the retired one by the time this fires, so a listener resolving it through [method wrapper_for_id] reads the same answer it will read for the rest of the cycle.

signal.name: entity_lingering
signal.description: Emitted by [method liveness_linger]. The wrapper stays live in the index, because a lingering entity is still resolvable.

signal.name: entity_live
signal.description: Emitted by [method liveness_publish_live], carrying the wrapper the index holds rather than one a caller passed alongside, so a listener resolves the same object the session will answer with for the rest of the route's life.

signal.name: kick_requested
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when a client asks for a peer to be kicked. Heard only by a session holding peer id 1. A payload that is not the target-and-reason pair names no target and is dropped rather than announced against a default one.

signal.name: kicked
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when server authority kicks this peer, before the transport closes. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: local_participant_joined
signal.description: Emitted by [method participant_publish_joined] when the joining peer is this one, ahead of [signal participant_joined], so a listener handling both sees itself arrive before it sees the roster grow.

signal.name: local_scene_changed
signal.description: Republishes the scene change of the participant this session decided is the local peer, bound when that row joins and released when the roster drops it. Another peer changing scene is not this session changing scene. The republished edge is the row's own [code]scene_changed[/code] signal, which [method participant_seat_move] and [method participant_seat_clear] emit. A seat written through [method participant_take_seat] or [method participant_leave_seat] reaches nobody here.

signal.name: local_player_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the entity representing this peer changes, including to [code]null[/code] when the route carrying it retires. Decided where a route goes live, because that is the only moment the answer can change, and read off the entity's own [NetwEntityRecord] rather than through the wrapper. A session with no transport represents nobody, which an offline session answering unique id 1 would otherwise look like.

signal.name: on_tick
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] during each tick. Primary simulation logic subscribes here.

signal.name: participant_joined
signal.description: Emitted by [method participant_publish_joined] for every admitted peer, this one included. A peer with no roster row has not been admitted and is never announced.

signal.name: peer_authenticating
signal.description: Republishes [signal SceneMultiplayer.peer_authenticating] from the transport this session holds. A transport the session replaces stops republishing at once.

signal.name: peer_authentication_failed
signal.description: Republishes [signal SceneMultiplayer.peer_authentication_failed] from the transport this session holds, after recording the refusal as a [code]PEER_AUTH_FAILED[/code] event, so a sink reads it in the order the session decided it.

signal.name: peer_packet
signal.description: Emitted by [method receive_header] for a datagram that is not Networked framing, so the application's own byte traffic reaches it over the same transport. A datagram that IS ours and is unreadable is never announced here.

signal.name: server_disconnecting
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when the server announces it is going away. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: scene_live
signal.description: Emitted by [method scene_publish_live] for the scene a newly live route belongs to. The handle is the one adopted for the container the publisher named, so a node inside a scene announces the scene and not itself.

signal.name: service_registered
signal.description: Emitted by [method service_register]. Announcing is part of registering rather than something a caller adds, so every door announces: the flat verb on the session and the registry's own both arrive at the same place. Re-registering the identical instance is inert and announces nothing.

signal.name: service_unregistered
signal.description: Emitted by [method service_unregister], and only when the type still names that service, so a service already replaced cannot unregister the one that replaced it.

signal.name: session_ended
signal.description: Announced by the session machine on leaving [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE], so a bring-up that failed before reaching it never announces an ending.

signal.name: session_entered
signal.description: Announced by the session machine on reaching [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE].

signal.name: session_reclaimed
signal.description: Announced immediately after [signal session_ended], so every listener of that signal has returned before this one fires. It is the phase, not a second ending. A listener that frees nodes the session owns binds here rather than on [signal session_ended], which is what keeps a listener of the announcement from being handed a node another listener already freed.

signal.name: poll_started
signal.description: Emitted by [method poll_delta], because marking a poll is what a poll starting is. [param delta] is the wall-clock gap since the previous mark, and zero on the session's first. A second reader in the same moment marked nothing and is announced nothing.

signal.name: stability_changed
signal.description: Announced by [member clock_handle] when [member NetwClockHandle.is_stable] flips, so a listener sees the transition rather than having to poll for it.

signal.name: state_changed
signal.description: Announced by the session machine on every legal edge. An edge it refuses is not a transition, so it is not published.

signal.name: table_received
signal.description: Emitted by [method table_publish] and [method table_publish_intake] for one table an intake touched or a commit produced. [param tick] is the one the commit stamped, so several commits inside one tick collapse to the last.

signal.name: tree_paused
signal.description: Emitted by [method session_publish_control] when server authority pauses the session. Pausing the engine is a subscriber's reaction rather than part of the decision, so the session announces the edge once and everything that reacts reads the same announcement. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: tree_unpaused
signal.description: The twin of [signal tree_paused].

constants.constant: No transport peer is assigned and none is being sought.
A peer is assigned and its connection is still in flight, so it may still fail back to [constant SESSION_STATE_OFFLINE] without ever announcing [signal session_entered].
The session carries traffic and [member role] is resolved. The only state [signal session_entered] and [signal session_ended] bracket.

Teardown is in flight. The session has left [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE], so it has already announced [signal session_ended], and it admits no new traffic on its way to [constant SESSION_STATE_OFFLINE].
No session, so no role has been resolved yet.
A remote peer holding no authority.
Server authority with no local player.
Server authority held by a peer that is also playing. Very little should test for [constant ROLE_CLIENT], because this role is a player too.
[method session_name_verdict] found the joining name free, or held by nobody this session refuses on behalf of. The join proceeds under the name it claimed.
The name collides and the join may be renamed around it, which is what a debug join asks for. The caller takes a free variant from [method session_free_name] and admits that.
The name collides and may not be altered, because it came from an authenticated identity. The join is rejected rather than renamed, so the roster never disagrees with the account behind it.
